text_marked: After this the Lord looked upon the earth, and filled it with his blessings.

text: With all manner of living things hath he covered the face thereof; and they shall return into it again.
text_marked: With all manner of living things hath he covered the face thereof; and they shall return into it again.

text: The Lord created man of the earth, and turned him into it again.
text_marked: The Lord created man of the earth, and turned him into it again.

text: He gave them few days, and a short time, and power also over the things therein.
text_marked: He gave them few days, and a short time, and power also over the things therein.

text: He endued them with strength by themselves, and made them according to his image,
text_marked: He endued them with strength by themselves, and made them according to his image,

text: And put the fear of man upon all flesh, and gave him dominion over beasts and fowls.
text_marked: And put the fear of man upon all flesh, and gave him dominion over beasts and fowls.

text: They received the use of the five operations of the Lord, and in the sixth place he imparted them understanding, and in the seventh speech, an interpreter of the cogitations thereof.
text_marked: They received the use of the five operations of the Lord, and in the sixth place he imparted them understanding, and in the seventh speech, an interpreter of the cogitations thereof.

text: Counsel, and a tongue, and eyes, ears, and a heart, gave he them to understand.
text_marked: Counsel, and a tongue, and eyes, ears, and a heart, gave he them to understand.

text: Withal he filled them with the knowledge of understanding, and shewed them good and evil.
text_marked: Withal he filled them with the knowledge of understanding, and shewed them good and evil.

text: He set his eye upon their hearts, that he might shew them the greatness of his works.
text_marked: He set his eye upon their hearts, that he might shew them the greatness of his works.

text: He gave them to glory in his marvellous acts for ever, that they might declare his works with understanding.
text_marked: He gave them to glory in his marvellous acts for ever, that they might declare his works with understanding.

text: And the elect shall praise his holy name.
text_marked: And the elect shall praise his holy name.

text: Beside this he gave them knowledge, and the law of life for an heritage.
text_marked: Beside this he gave them knowledge, and the law of life for an heritage.

text: He made an everlasting covenant with them, and shewed them his judgments.
text_marked: He made an everlasting covenant with them, and shewed them his judgments.

text: Their eyes saw the majesty of his glory, and their ears heard his glorious voice.
text_marked: Their eyes saw the majesty of his glory, and their ears heard his glorious voice.

text: And he said unto them, Beware of all unrighteousness; and he gave every man commandment concerning his neighbour.
text_marked: And he said unto them, Beware of all unrighteousness; and he gave every man commandment concerning his neighbour.

text: Their ways are ever before him, and shall not be hid from his eyes.
text_marked: Their ways are ever before him, and shall not be hid from his eyes.

text: Every man from his youth is given to evil; neither could they make to themselves fleshy hearts for stony.
text_marked: Every man from his youth is given to evil; neither could they make to themselves fleshy hearts for stony.

text: For in the division of the nations of the whole earth he set a ruler over every people; but Israel is the Lord’s portion:
text_marked: For in the division of the nations of the whole earth he set a ruler over every people; but Israel is the Lord’s portion:

text: Whom, being his firstborn, he nourisheth with discipline, and giving him the light of his love doth not forsake him.
text_marked: Whom, being his firstborn, he nourisheth with discipline, and giving him the light of his love doth not forsake him.

text: Therefore all their works are as the sun before him, and his eyes are continually upon their ways.
text_marked: Therefore all their works are as the sun before him, and his eyes are continually upon their ways.

text: None of their unrighteous deeds are hid from him, but all their sins are before the Lord
text_marked: None of their unrighteous deeds are hid from him, but all their sins are before the Lord

text: But the Lord being gracious and knowing his workmanship, neither left nor forsook them, but spared them.
text_marked: But the Lord being gracious and knowing his workmanship, neither left nor forsook them, but spared them.

text: The alms of a man is as a signet with him, and he will keep the good deeds of man as the apple of the eye, and give repentance to his sons and daughters.
text_marked: The alms of a man is as a signet with him, and he will keep the good deeds of man as the apple of the eye, and give repentance to his sons and daughters.

text: Afterwards he will rise up and reward them, and render their recompence upon their heads.
text_marked: Afterwards he will rise up and reward them, and render their recompence upon their heads.

text: But unto them that repent, he granted them return, and comforted those that failed in patience.
text_marked: But unto them that repent, he granted them return, and comforted those that failed in patience.

text: Return unto the Lord, and forsake thy sins, make thy prayer before his face, and offend less.
text_marked: Return unto the Lord, and forsake thy sins, make thy prayer before his face, and offend less.

text: Turn again to the most High, and turn away from iniquity: for he will lead thee out of darkness into the light of health, and hate thou abomination vehemently.
text_marked: Turn again to the most High, and turn away from iniquity: for he will lead thee out of darkness into the light of health, and hate thou abomination vehemently.

text: Who shall praise the most High in the grave, instead of them which live and give thanks?
text_marked: Who shall praise the most High in the grave, instead of them which live and give thanks?

text: Thanksgiving perisheth from the dead, as from one that is not: the living and sound in heart shall praise the Lord.
text_marked: Thanksgiving perisheth from the dead, as from one that is not: the living and sound in heart shall praise the Lord.

text: How great is the lovingkindness of the Lord our God, and his compassion unto such as turn unto him in holiness!
text_marked: How great is the lovingkindness of the Lord our God, and his compassion unto such as turn unto him in holiness!

text: For all things cannot be in men, because the son of man is not immortal.
text_marked: For all things cannot be in men, because the son of man is not immortal.

text: What is brighter than the sun? yet the light thereof faileth; and flesh and blood will imagine evil.
text_marked: What is brighter than the sun? yet the light thereof faileth; and flesh and blood will imagine evil.

text: He vieweth the power of the height of heaven; and all men are but earth and ashes.
text_marked: He vieweth the power of the height of heaven; and all men are but earth and ashes.

text: He that liveth for ever Hath created all things in general.
text_marked: He that liveth for ever Hath created all things in general.

text: The Lord only is righteous, and there is none other but he,
text_marked: The Lord only is righteous, and there is none other but he,

text: Who governeth the world with the palm of his hand, and all things obey his will: for he is the King of all, by his power dividing holy things among them from profane.
text_marked: Who governeth the world with the palm of his hand, and all things obey his will: for he is the King of all, by his power dividing holy things among them from profane.

text: To whom hath he given power to declare his works? and who shall find out his noble acts?
text_marked: To whom hath he given power to declare his works? and who shall find out his noble acts?

text: Who shall number the strength of his majesty? and who shall also tell out his mercies?
text_marked: Who shall number the strength of his majesty? and who shall also tell out his mercies?

text: As for the wondrous works of the Lord, there may nothing be taken from them, neither may any thing be put unto them, neither can the ground of them be found out.
text_marked: As for the wondrous works of the Lord, there may nothing be taken from them, neither may any thing be put unto them, neither can the ground of them be found out.

text: When a man hath done, then he beginneth; and when he leaveth off, then he shall be doubtful.
text_marked: When a man hath done, then he beginneth; and when he leaveth off, then he shall be doubtful.

text: What is man, and whereto serveth he? what is his good, and what is his evil?
text_marked: What is man, and whereto serveth he? what is his good, and what is his evil?

text: The number of a man’s days at the most are an hundred years.
text_marked: The number of a man’s days at the most are an hundred years.

text: As a drop of water unto the sea, and a gravelstone in comparison of the sand; so are a thousand years to the days of eternity.
text_marked: As a drop of water unto the sea, and a gravelstone in comparison of the sand; so are a thousand years to the days of eternity.

text: Therefore is God patient with them, and poureth forth his mercy upon them.
text_marked: Therefore is God patient with them, and poureth forth his mercy upon them.

text: He saw and perceived their end to be evil; therefore he multiplied his compassion.
text_marked: He saw and perceived their end to be evil; therefore he multiplied his compassion.

text: The mercy of man is toward his neighbour; but the mercy of the Lord is upon all flesh: he reproveth, and nurtureth, and teacheth and bringeth again, as a shepherd his flock.
text_marked: The mercy of man is toward his neighbour; but the mercy of the Lord is upon all flesh: he reproveth, and nurtureth, and teacheth and bringeth again, as a shepherd his flock.

text: He hath mercy on them that receive discipline, and that diligently seek after his judgments.
text_marked: He hath mercy on them that receive discipline, and that diligently seek after his judgments.

text: My son, blemish not thy good deeds, neither use uncomfortable words when thou givest any thing.
text_marked: My son, blemish not thy good deeds, neither use uncomfortable words when thou givest any thing.

text: Shall not the dew asswage the heat? so is a word better than a gift.
text_marked: Shall not the dew asswage the heat? so is a word better than a gift.

text: Lo, is not a word better than a gift? but both are with a gracious man.
text_marked: Lo, is not a word better than a gift? but both are with a gracious man.

text: A fool will upbraid churlishly, and a gift of the envious consumeth the eyes.
text_marked: A fool will upbraid churlishly, and a gift of the envious consumeth the eyes.

text: Learn before thou speak, and use physick or ever thou be sick.
text_marked: Learn before thou speak, and use physick or ever thou be sick.

text: Before judgment examine thyself, and in the day of visitation thou shalt find mercy.
text_marked: Before judgment examine thyself, and in the day of visitation thou shalt find mercy.

text: Humble thyself before thou be sick, and in the time of sins shew repentance.
text_marked: Humble thyself before thou be sick, and in the time of sins shew repentance.

text: Let nothing hinder thee to pay thy vow in due time, and defer not until death to be justified.
text_marked: Let nothing hinder thee to pay thy vow in due time, and defer not until death to be justified.

text: Before thou prayest, prepare thyself; and be not as one that tempteth the Lord.
text_marked: Before thou prayest, prepare thyself; and be not as one that tempteth the Lord.

text: Think upon the wrath that shall be at the end, and the time of vengeance, when he shall turn away his face.
text_marked: Think upon the wrath that shall be at the end, and the time of vengeance, when he shall turn away his face.

text: When thou hast enough, remember the time of hunger: and when thou art rich, think upon poverty and need.
text_marked: When thou hast enough, remember the time of hunger: and when thou art rich, think upon poverty and need.

text: From the morning until the evening the time is changed, and all things are soon done before the Lord.
text_marked: From the morning until the evening the time is changed, and all things are soon done before the Lord.

text: A wise man will fear in every thing, and in the day of sinning he will beware of offence: but a fool will not observe time.
text_marked: A wise man will fear in every thing, and in the day of sinning he will beware of offence: but a fool will not observe time.

text: Every man of understanding knoweth wisdom, and will give praise unto him that found her.
text_marked: Every man of understanding knoweth wisdom, and will give praise unto him that found her.

text: They that were of understanding in sayings became also wise themselves, and poured forth exquisite parables.
text_marked: They that were of understanding in sayings became also wise themselves, and poured forth exquisite parables.

text: Go not after thy lusts, but refrain thyself from thine appetites.
text_marked: Go not after thy lusts, but refrain thyself from thine appetites.

text: If thou givest thy soul the desires that please her, she will make thee a laughingstock to thine enemies that malign thee.
text_marked: If thou givest thy soul the desires that please her, she will make thee a laughingstock to thine enemies that malign thee.

text: Take not pleasure in much good cheer, neither be tied to the expence thereof.
text_marked: Take not pleasure in much good cheer, neither be tied to the expence thereof.

text: Be not made a beggar by banqueting upon borrowing, when thou hast nothing in thy purse: for thou shalt lie in wait for thine own life, and be talked on.
text_marked: Be not made a beggar by banqueting upon borrowing, when thou hast nothing in thy purse: for thou shalt lie in wait for thine own life, and be talked on.

text: A labouring man that is given to drunkenness shall not be rich: and he that contemneth small things shall fall by little and little.
text_marked: A labouring man that is given to drunkenness shall not be rich: and he that contemneth small things shall fall by little and little.

text: Wine and women will make men of understanding to fall away: and he that cleaveth to harlots will become impudent.
text_marked: Wine and women will make men of understanding to fall away: and he that cleaveth to harlots will become impudent.

text: Moths and worms shall have him to heritage, and a bold man shall be taken away.
text_marked: Moths and worms shall have him to heritage, and a bold man shall be taken away.

text: He that is hasty to give credit is lightminded; and he that sinneth shall offend against his own soul.
text_marked: He that is hasty to give credit is lightminded; and he that sinneth shall offend against his own soul.

text: Whoso taketh pleasure in wickedness shall be condemned: but he that resisteth pleasures crowneth his life.
text_marked: Whoso taketh pleasure in wickedness shall be condemned: but he that resisteth pleasures crowneth his life.

text: He that can rule his tongue shall live without strife; and he that hateth babbling shall have less evil.
text_marked: He that can rule his tongue shall live without strife; and he that hateth babbling shall have less evil.

text: Rehearse not unto another that which is told unto thee, and thou shalt fare never the worse.
text_marked: Rehearse not unto another that which is told unto thee, and thou shalt fare never the worse.

text: Whether it be to friend or foe, talk not of other men’s lives; and if thou canst without offence, reveal them not.
text_marked: Whether it be to friend or foe, talk not of other men’s lives; and if thou canst without offence, reveal them not.

text: For he heard and observed thee, and when time cometh he will hate thee.
text_marked: For he heard and observed thee, and when time cometh he will hate thee.

text: If thou hast heard a word, let it die with thee; and be bold, it will not burst thee.
text_marked: If thou hast heard a word, let it die with thee; and be bold, it will not burst thee.

text: A fool travaileth with a word, as a woman in labour of a child.
text_marked: A fool travaileth with a word, as a woman in labour of a child.

text: As an arrow that sticketh in a man’s thigh, so is a word within a fool’s belly.
text_marked: As an arrow that sticketh in a man’s thigh, so is a word within a fool’s belly.

text: Admonish a friend, it may be he hath not done it: and if he have done it, that he do it no more.
text_marked: Admonish a friend, it may be he hath not done it: and if he have done it, that he do it no more.

text: Admonish thy friend, it may be he hath not said it: and if he have, that he speak it not again.
text_marked: Admonish thy friend, it may be he hath not said it: and if he have, that he speak it not again.

text: Admonish a friend: for many times it is a slander, and believe not every tale.
text_marked: Admonish a friend: for many times it is a slander, and believe not every tale.

text: There is one that slippeth in his speech, but not from his heart; and who is he that hath not offended with his tongue?
text_marked: There is one that slippeth in his speech, but not from his heart; and who is he that hath not offended with his tongue?

text: Admonish thy neighbour before thou threaten him; and not being angry, give place to the law of the most High.
text_marked: Admonish thy neighbour before thou threaten him; and not being angry, give place to the law of the most High.

text: The fear of the Lord is the first step to be accepted of him, and wisdom obtaineth his love.
text_marked: The fear of the Lord is the first step to be accepted [of him], and wisdom obtaineth his love.

text: The knowledge of the commandments of the Lord is the doctrine of life: and they that do things that please him shall receive the fruit of the tree of immortality.
text_marked: The knowledge of the commandments of the Lord is the doctrine of life: and they that do things that please him shall receive the fruit of the tree of immortality.

text: The fear of the Lord is all wisdom; and in all wisdom is the performance of the law, and the knowledge of his omnipotency.
text_marked: The fear of the Lord is all wisdom; and in all wisdom is the performance of the law, and the knowledge of his omnipotency.

text: If a servant say to his master, I will not do as it pleaseth thee; though afterward he do it, he angereth him that nourisheth him.
text_marked: If a servant say to his master, I will not do as it pleaseth thee; though afterward he do it, he angereth him that nourisheth him.

text: The knowledge of wickedness is not wisdom, neither at any time the counsel of sinners prudence.
text_marked: The knowledge of wickedness is not wisdom, neither at any time the counsel of sinners prudence.

text: There is a wickedness, and the same an abomination; and there is a fool wanting in wisdom.
text_marked: There is a wickedness, and the same an abomination; and there is a fool wanting in wisdom.

text: He that hath small understanding, and feareth God, is better than one that hath much wisdom, and transgresseth the law of the most High.
text_marked: He that hath small understanding, and feareth God, is better than one that hath much wisdom, and transgresseth the law of the most High.

text: There is an exquisite subtilty, and the same is unjust; and there is one that turneth aside to make judgment appear; and there is a wise man that justifieth in judgment.
text_marked: There is an exquisite subtilty, and the same is unjust; and there is one that turneth aside to make judgment appear; and there is a wise man that justifieth in judgment.

text: There is a wicked man that hangeth down his head sadly; but inwardly he is full of deceit,
text_marked: There is a wicked man that hangeth down his head sadly; but inwardly he is full of deceit,

text: Casting down his countenance, and making as if he heard not: where he is not known, he will do thee a mischief before thou be aware.
text_marked: Casting down his countenance, and making as if he heard not: where he is not known, he will do thee a mischief before thou be aware.

text: And if for want of power he be hindered from sinning, yet when he findeth opportunity he will do evil.
text_marked: And if for want of power he be hindered from sinning, yet when he findeth opportunity he will do evil.

text: A man may be known by his look, and one that hath understanding by his countenance, when thou meetest him.
text_marked: A man may be known by his look, and one that hath understanding by his countenance, when thou meetest him.

text: A man’s attire, and excessive laughter, and gait, shew what he is.
text_marked: A man’s attire, and excessive laughter, and gait, shew what he is.

text: There is a reproof that is not comely: again, some man holdeth his tongue, and he is wise.
text_marked: There is a reproof that is not comely: again, some man holdeth his tongue, and he is wise.

text: It is much better to reprove, than to be angry secretly: and he that confesseth his fault shall be preserved from hurt.
text_marked: It is much better to reprove, than to be angry secretly: and he that confesseth his fault shall be preserved from hurt.

text: How good is it, when thou art reproved, to shew repentance! for so shalt thou escape wilful sin.
text_marked: How good is it, when thou art reproved, to shew repentance! for so shalt thou escape wilful sin.

text: As is the lust of an eunuch to deflower a virgin; so is he that executeth judgment with violence.
text_marked: As is the lust of an eunuch to deflower a virgin; so is he that executeth judgment with violence.

text: There is one that keepeth silence, and is found wise: and another by much babbling becometh hateful.
text_marked: There is one that keepeth silence, and is found wise: and another by much babbling becometh hateful.

text: Some man holdeth his tongue, because he hath not to answer: and some keepeth silence, knowing his time.
text_marked: Some man holdeth his tongue, because he hath not to answer: and some keepeth silence, knowing his time.

text: A wise man will hold his tongue till he see opportunity: but a babbler and a fool will regard no time.
text_marked: A wise man will hold his tongue till he see opportunity: but a babbler and a fool will regard no time.

text: He that useth many words shall be abhorred; and he that taketh to himself authority therein shall be hated.
text_marked: He that useth many words shall be abhorred; and he that taketh to himself authority therein shall be hated.

text: There is a sinner that hath good success in evil things; and there is a gain that turneth to loss.
text_marked: There is a sinner that hath good success in evil things; and there is a gain that turneth to loss.

text: There is a gift that shall not profit thee; and there is a gift whose recompence is double.
text_marked: There is a gift that shall not profit thee; and there is a gift whose recompence is double.

text: There is an abasement because of glory; and there is that lifteth up his head from a low estate.
text_marked: There is an abasement because of glory; and there is that lifteth up his head from a low estate.

text: There is that buyeth much for a little, and repayeth it sevenfold.
text_marked: There is that buyeth much for a little, and repayeth it sevenfold.

text: A wise man by his words maketh him beloved: but the graces of fools shall be poured out.
text_marked: A wise man by his words maketh him beloved: but the graces of fools shall be poured out.

text: The gift of a fool shall do thee no good when thou hast it; neither yet of the envious for his necessity: for he looketh to receive many things for one.
text_marked: The gift of a fool shall do thee no good when thou hast it; neither yet of the envious for his necessity: for he looketh to receive many things for one.

text: He giveth little, and upbraideth much; he openeth his mouth like a crier; to day he lendeth, and to morrow will he ask it again: such an one is to be hated of God and man.
text_marked: He giveth little, and upbraideth much; he openeth his mouth like a crier; to day he lendeth, and to morrow will he ask it again: such an one is to be hated of God and man.

text: The fool saith, I have no friends, I have no thank for all my good deeds, and they that eat my bread speak evil of me.
text_marked: The fool saith, I have no friends, I have no thank for all my good deeds, and they that eat my bread speak evil of me.

text: How oft, and of how many shall he be laughed to scorn! for he knoweth not aright what it is to have; and it is all one unto him as if he had it not.
text_marked: How oft, and of how many shall he be laughed to scorn! for he knoweth not aright what it is to have; and it is all one unto him as if he had it not.

text: To slip upon a pavement is better than to slip with the tongue: so the fall of the wicked shall come speedily.
text_marked: To slip upon a pavement is better than to slip with the tongue: so the fall of the wicked shall come speedily.

text: An unseasonable tale will always be in the mouth of the unwise.
text_marked: An unseasonable tale will always be in the mouth of the unwise.

text: A wise sentence shall be rejected when it cometh out of a fool’s mouth; for he will not speak it in due season.
text_marked: A wise sentence shall be rejected when it cometh out of a fool’s mouth; for he will not speak it in due season.

text: There is that is hindered from sinning through want: and when he taketh rest, he shall not be troubled.
text_marked: There is that is hindered from sinning through want: and when he taketh rest, he shall not be troubled.

text: There is that destroyeth his own soul through bashfulness, and by accepting of persons overthroweth himself.
text_marked: There is that destroyeth his own soul through bashfulness, and by accepting of persons overthroweth himself.

text: There is that for bashfulness promiseth to his friend, and maketh him his enemy for nothing.
text_marked: There is that for bashfulness promiseth to his friend, and maketh him his enemy for nothing.

text: A lie is a foul blot in a man, yet it is continually in the mouth of the untaught.
text_marked: A lie is a foul blot in a man, yet it is continually in the mouth of the untaught.

text: A thief is better than a man that is accustomed to lie: but they both shall have destruction to heritage.
text_marked: A thief is better than a man that is accustomed to lie: but they both shall have destruction to heritage.

text: The disposition of a liar is dishonourable, and his shame is ever with him.
text_marked: The disposition of a liar is dishonourable, and his shame is ever with him.

text: A wise man shall promote himself to honour with his words: and he that hath understanding will please great men.
text_marked: A wise man shall promote himself to honour with his words: and he that hath understanding will please great men.

text: He that tilleth his land shall increase his heap: and he that pleaseth great men shall get pardon for iniquity.
text_marked: He that tilleth his land shall increase his heap: and he that pleaseth great men shall get pardon for iniquity.

text: Presents and gifts blind the eyes of the wise, and stop up his mouth that he cannot reprove.
text_marked: Presents and gifts blind the eyes of the wise, and stop up his mouth that he cannot reprove.

text: Wisdom that is hid, and treasure that is hoarded up, what profit is in them both?
text_marked: Wisdom that is hid, and treasure that is hoarded up, what profit is in them both?

text: Better is he that hideth his folly than a man that hideth his wisdom.
text_marked: Better is he that hideth his folly than a man that hideth his wisdom.

text: Necessary patience in seeking the Lord is better than he that leadeth his life without a guide.
text_marked: Necessary patience in seeking the Lord is better than he that leadeth his life without a guide.

text: My son, hast thou sinned? do so no more, but ask pardon for thy former sins.
text_marked: My son, hast thou sinned? do so no more, but ask pardon for thy former sins.

text: Flee from sin as from the face of a serpent: for if thou comest too near it, it will bite thee: the teeth thereof are as the teeth of a lion, slaying the souls of men.
text_marked: Flee from sin as from the face of a serpent: for if thou comest too near it, it will bite thee: the teeth thereof are as the teeth of a lion, slaying the souls of men.

text: All iniquity is as a two edged sword, the wounds whereof cannot be healed.
text_marked: All iniquity is as a two edged sword, the wounds whereof cannot be healed.

text: To terrify and do wrong will waste riches: thus the house of proud men shall be made desolate.
text_marked: To terrify and do wrong will waste riches: thus the house of proud men shall be made desolate.

text: A prayer out of a poor man’s mouth reacheth to the ears of God, and his judgment cometh speedily.
text_marked: A prayer out of a poor man’s mouth reacheth to the ears of God, and his judgment cometh speedily.

text: He that hateth to be reproved is in the way of sinners: but he that feareth the Lord will repent from his heart.
text_marked: He that hateth to be reproved is in the way of sinners: but he that feareth the Lord will repent from his heart.

text: An eloquent man is known far and near; but a man of understanding knoweth when he slippeth.
text_marked: An eloquent man is known far and near; but a man of understanding knoweth when he slippeth.

text: He that buildeth his house with other men’s money is like one that gathereth himself stones for the tomb of his burial.
text_marked: He that buildeth his house with other men’s money is like one that gathereth himself stones for the tomb of his burial.

text: The congregation of the wicked is like tow wrapped together: and the end of them is a flame of fire to destroy them.
text_marked: The congregation of the wicked is like tow wrapped together: and the end of them is a flame of fire to destroy them.

text: The way of sinners is made plain with stones, but at the end thereof is the pit of hell.
text_marked: The way of sinners is made plain with stones, but at the end thereof is the pit of hell.

text: He that keepeth the law of the Lord getteth the understanding thereof: and the perfection of the fear of the Lord is wisdom.
text_marked: He that keepeth the law of the Lord getteth the understanding thereof: and the perfection of the fear of the Lord is wisdom.

text: He that is not wise will not be taught: but there is a wisdom which multiplieth bitterness.
text_marked: He that is not wise will not be taught: but there is a wisdom which multiplieth bitterness.

text: The knowledge of a wise man shall abound like a flood: and his counsel is like a pure fountain of life.
text_marked: The knowledge of a wise man shall abound like a flood: and his counsel is like a pure fountain of life.

text: The inner parts of a fool are like a broken vessel, and he will hold no knowledge as long as he liveth.
text_marked: The inner parts of a fool are like a broken vessel, and he will hold no knowledge as long as he liveth.

text: If a skilful man hear a wise word, he will commend it, and add unto it: but as soon as one of no understanding heareth it, it displeaseth him, and he casteth it behind his back.
text_marked: If a skilful man hear a wise word, he will commend it, and add unto it: but as soon as one of no understanding heareth it, it displeaseth him, and he casteth it behind his back.

text: The talking of a fool is like a burden in the way: but grace shall be found in the lips of the wise.
text_marked: The talking of a fool is like a burden in the way: but grace shall be found in the lips of the wise.

text: They enquire at the mouth of the wise man in the congregation, and they shall ponder his words in their heart.
text_marked: They enquire at the mouth of the wise man in the congregation, and they shall ponder his words in their heart.

text: As is a house that is destroyed, so is wisdom to a fool: and the knowledge of the unwise is as talk without sense.
text_marked: As is a house that is destroyed, so is wisdom to a fool: and the knowledge of the unwise is as talk without sense.

text: Doctrine unto fools is as fetters on the feet, and like manacles on the right hand.
text_marked: Doctrine unto fools is as fetters on the feet, and like manacles on the right hand.

text: A fool lifteth up his voice with laughter; but a wise man doth scarce smile a little.
text_marked: A fool lifteth up his voice with laughter; but a wise man doth scarce smile a little.

text: Learning is unto a wise man as an ornament of gold, and like a bracelet upon his right arm.
text_marked: Learning is unto a wise man as an ornament of gold, and like a bracelet upon his right arm.

text: A foolish man’s foot is soon in his neighbour’s house: but a man of experience is ashamed of him.
text_marked: A foolish man’s foot is soon in his [neighbour’s] house: but a man of experience is ashamed of him.

text: A fool will peep in at the door into the house: but he that is well nurtured will stand without.
text_marked: A fool will peep in at the door into the house: but he that is well nurtured will stand without.

text: It is the rudeness of a man to hearken at the door: but a wise man will be grieved with the disgrace.
text_marked: It is the rudeness of a man to hearken at the door: but a wise man will be grieved with the disgrace.

text: The lips of talkers will be telling such things as pertain not unto them: but the words of such as have understanding are weighed in the balance.
text_marked: The lips of talkers will be telling such things as pertain not unto them: but the words of such as have understanding are weighed in the balance.

text: The heart of fools is in their mouth: but the mouth of the wise is in their heart.
text_marked: The heart of fools is in their mouth: but the mouth of the wise is in their heart.

text: When the ungodly curseth Satan, he curseth his own soul.
text_marked: When the ungodly curseth Satan, he curseth his own soul.

text: A whisperer defileth his own soul, and is hated wheresoever he dwelleth.
text_marked: A whisperer defileth his own soul, and is hated wheresoever he dwelleth.

text: A slothful man is compared to a filthy stone, and every one will hiss him out to his disgrace.
text_marked: A slothful man is compared to a filthy stone, and every one will hiss him out to his disgrace.

text: A slothful man is compared to the filth of a dunghill: every man that takes it up will shake his hand.
text_marked: A slothful man is compared to the filth of a dunghill: every man that takes it up will shake his hand.

text: An evilnurtured man is the dishonour of his father that begat him: and a foolish daughter is born to his loss.
text_marked: An evilnurtured man is the dishonour of his father that begat him: and a [foolish] daughter is born to his loss.

text: A wise daughter shall bring an inheritance to her husband: but she that liveth dishonestly is her father’s heaviness.
text_marked: A wise daughter shall bring an inheritance to her husband: but she that liveth dishonestly is her father’s heaviness.

text: She that is bold dishonoureth both her father and her husband, but they both shall despise her.
text_marked: She that is bold dishonoureth both her father and her husband, but they both shall despise her.

text: A tale out of season is as musick in mourning: but stripes and correction of wisdom are never out of time.
text_marked: A tale out of season [is as] musick in mourning: but stripes and correction of wisdom are never out of time.

text: Whoso teacheth a fool is as one that glueth a potsherd together, and as he that waketh one from a sound sleep.
text_marked: Whoso teacheth a fool is as one that glueth a potsherd together, and as he that waketh one from a sound sleep.

text: He that telleth a tale to a fool speaketh to one in a slumber: when he hath told his tale, he will say, What is the matter?
text_marked: He that telleth a tale to a fool speaketh to one in a slumber: when he hath told his tale, he will say, What is the matter?

text: If children live honestly, and have wherewithal, they shall cover the baseness of their parents.
text_marked: If children live honestly, and have wherewithal, they shall cover the baseness of their parents.

text: But children, being haughty, through disdain and want of nurture do stain the nobility of their kindred.
text_marked: But children, being haughty, through disdain and want of nurture do stain the nobility of their kindred.

text: Weep for the dead, for he hath lost the light: and weep for the fool, for he wanteth understanding: make little weeping for the dead, for he is at rest: but the life of the fool is worse than death.
text_marked: Weep for the dead, for he hath lost the light: and weep for the fool, for he wanteth understanding: make little weeping for the dead, for he is at rest: but the life of the fool is worse than death.

text: Seven days do men mourn for him that is dead; but for a fool and an ungodly man all the days of his life.
text_marked: Seven days do men mourn for him that is dead; but for a fool and an ungodly man all the days of his life.

text: Talk not much with a fool, and go not to him that hath no understanding: beware of him, lest thou have trouble, and thou shalt never be defiled with his fooleries: depart from him, and thou shalt find rest, and never be disquieted with madness.
text_marked: Talk not much with a fool, and go not to him that hath no understanding: beware of him, lest thou have trouble, and thou shalt never be defiled with his fooleries: depart from him, and thou shalt find rest, and never be disquieted with madness.

text: What is heavier than lead? and what is the name thereof, but a fool?
text_marked: What is heavier than lead? and what is the name thereof, but a fool?

text: Sand, and salt, and a mass of iron, is easier to bear, than a man without understanding.
text_marked: Sand, and salt, and a mass of iron, is easier to bear, than a man without understanding.

text: As timber girt and bound together in a building cannot be loosed with shaking: so the heart that is stablished by advised counsel shall fear at no time.
text_marked: As timber girt and bound together in a building cannot be loosed with shaking: so the heart that is stablished by advised counsel shall fear at no time.

text: A heart settled upon a thought of understanding is as a fair plaistering on the wall of a gallery.
text_marked: A heart settled upon a thought of understanding is as a fair plaistering on the wall of a gallery.

text: Pales set on an high place will never stand against the wind: so a fearful heart in the imagination of a fool cannot stand against any fear.
text_marked: Pales set on an high place will never stand against the wind: so a fearful heart in the imagination of a fool cannot stand against any fear.

text: He that pricketh the eye will make tears to fall: and he that pricketh the heart maketh it to shew her knowledge.
text_marked: He that pricketh the eye will make tears to fall: and he that pricketh the heart maketh it to shew her knowledge.

text: Whoso casteth a stone at the birds frayeth them away: and he that upbraideth his friend breaketh friendship.
text_marked: Whoso casteth a stone at the birds frayeth them away: and he that upbraideth his friend breaketh friendship.

text: Though thou drewest a sword at thy friend, yet despair not: for there may be a returning to favour.
text_marked: Though thou drewest a sword at thy friend, yet despair not: for there may be a returning [to favour].

text: If thou hast opened thy mouth against thy friend, fear not; for there may be a reconciliation: except for upbraiding, or pride, or disclosing of secrets, or a treacherous wound: for for these things every friend will depart.
text_marked: If thou hast opened thy mouth against thy friend, fear not; for there may be a reconciliation: except for upbraiding, or pride, or disclosing of secrets, or a treacherous wound: for for these things every friend will depart.

text: Be faithful to thy neighbour in his poverty, that thou mayest rejoice in his prosperity: abide stedfast unto him in the time of his trouble, that thou mayest be heir with him in his heritage: for a mean estate is not always to be contemned: nor the rich that is foolish to be had in admiration.
text_marked: Be faithful to thy neighbour in his poverty, that thou mayest rejoice in his prosperity: abide stedfast unto him in the time of his trouble, that thou mayest be heir with him in his heritage: for a mean estate is not always to be contemned: nor the rich that is foolish to be had in admiration.

text: As the vapour and smoke of a furnace goeth before the fire; so reviling before blood.
text_marked: As the vapour and smoke of a furnace goeth before the fire; so reviling before blood.

text: I will not be ashamed to defend a friend; neither will I hide myself from him.
text_marked: I will not be ashamed to defend a friend; neither will I hide myself from him.

text: And if any evil happen unto me by him, every one that heareth it will beware of him.
text_marked: And if any evil happen unto me by him, every one that heareth it will beware of him.

text: Who shall set a watch before my mouth, and a seal of wisdom upon my lips, that I fall not suddenly by them, and that my tongue destroy me not?
text_marked: Who shall set a watch before my mouth, and a seal of wisdom upon my lips, that I fall not suddenly by them, and that my tongue destroy me not?

text: O Lord, Father and Governor of all my whole life, leave me not to their counsels, and let me not fall by them.
text_marked: O Lord, Father and Governor of all my whole life, leave me not to their counsels, and let me not fall by them.

text: Who will set scourges over my thoughts, and the discipline of wisdom over mine heart? that they spare me not for mine ignorances, and it pass not by my sins:
text_marked: Who will set scourges over my thoughts, and the discipline of wisdom over mine heart? that they spare me not for mine ignorances, and it pass not by my sins:

text: Lest mine ignorances increase, and my sins abound to my destruction, and I fall before mine adversaries, and mine enemy rejoice over me, whose hope is far from thy mercy.
text_marked: Lest mine ignorances increase, and my sins abound to my destruction, and I fall before mine adversaries, and mine enemy rejoice over me, whose hope is far from thy mercy.

text: O Lord, Father and God of my life, give me not a proud look, but turn away from thy servants always a haughty mind.
text_marked: O Lord, Father and God of my life, give me not a proud look, but turn away from thy servants always a haughty mind.

text: Turn away from me vain hopes and concupiscence, and thou shalt hold him up that is desirous always to serve thee.
text_marked: Turn away from me vain hopes and concupiscence, and thou shalt hold him up that is desirous always to serve thee.

text: Let not the greediness of the belly nor lust of the flesh take hold of me; and give not over me thy servant into an impudent mind.
text_marked: Let not the greediness of the belly nor lust of the flesh take hold of me; and give not over me thy servant into an impudent mind.

text: Hear, O ye children, the discipline of the mouth: he that keepeth it shall never be taken in his lips.
text_marked: Hear, O ye children, the discipline of the mouth: he that keepeth it shall never be taken in his lips.

text: The sinner shall be left in his foolishness: both the evil speaker and the proud shall fall thereby.
text_marked: The sinner shall be left in his foolishness: both the evil speaker and the proud shall fall thereby.

text: Accustom not thy mouth to swearing; neither use thyself to the naming of the Holy One.
text_marked: Accustom not thy mouth to swearing; neither use thyself to the naming of the Holy One.

text: For as a servant that is continually beaten shall not be without a blue mark: so he that sweareth and nameth God continually shall not be faultless.
text_marked: For as a servant that is continually beaten shall not be without a blue mark: so he that sweareth and nameth God continually shall not be faultless.

text: A man that useth much swearing shall be filled with iniquity, and the plague shall never depart from his house: if he shall offend, his sin shall be upon him: and if he acknowledge not his sin, he maketh a double offence: and if he swear in vain, he shall not be innocent, but his house shall be full of calamities.
text_marked: A man that useth much swearing shall be filled with iniquity, and the plague shall never depart from his house: if he shall offend, his sin shall be upon him: and if he acknowledge not his sin, he maketh a double offence: and if he swear in vain, he shall not be innocent, but his house shall be full of calamities.

text: There is a word that is clothed about with death: God grant that it be not found in the heritage of Jacob; for all such things shall be far from the godly, and they shall not wallow in their sins.
text_marked: There is a word that is clothed about with death: God grant that it be not found in the heritage of Jacob; for all such things shall be far from the godly, and they shall not wallow in their sins.

text: Use not thy mouth to intemperate swearing, for therein is the word of sin.
text_marked: Use not thy mouth to intemperate swearing, for therein is the word of sin.

text: Remember thy father and thy mother, when thou sittest among great men. Be not forgetful before them, and so thou by thy custom become a fool, and wish that thou hadst not been born, and curse they day of thy nativity.
text_marked: Remember thy father and thy mother, when thou sittest among great men. Be not forgetful before them, and so thou by thy custom become a fool, and wish that thou hadst not been born, and curse they day of thy nativity.

text: The man that is accustomed to opprobrious words will never be reformed all the days of his life.
text_marked: The man that is accustomed to opprobrious words will never be reformed all the days of his life.

text: Two sorts of men multiply sin, and the third will bring wrath: a hot mind is as a burning fire, it will never be quenched till it be consumed: a fornicator in the body of his flesh will never cease till he hath kindled a fire.
text_marked: Two sorts of men multiply sin, and the third will bring wrath: a hot mind is as a burning fire, it will never be quenched till it be consumed: a fornicator in the body of his flesh will never cease till he hath kindled a fire.

text: All bread is sweet to a whoremonger, he will not leave off till he die.
text_marked: All bread is sweet to a whoremonger, he will not leave off till he die.

text: A man that breaketh wedlock, saying thus in his heart, Who seeth me? I am compassed about with darkness, the walls cover me, and no body seeth me; what need I to fear? the most High will not remember my sins:
text_marked: A man that breaketh wedlock, saying thus in his heart, Who seeth me? I am compassed about with darkness, the walls cover me, and no body seeth me; what need I to fear? the most High will not remember my sins:

text: Such a man only feareth the eyes of men, and knoweth not that the eyes of the Lord are ten thousand times brighter than the sun, beholding all the ways of men, and considering the most secret parts.
text_marked: Such a man only feareth the eyes of men, and knoweth not that the eyes of the Lord are ten thousand times brighter than the sun, beholding all the ways of men, and considering the most secret parts.

text: He knew all things ere ever they were created; so also after they were perfected he looked upon them all.
text_marked: He knew all things ere ever they were created; so also after they were perfected he looked upon them all.

text: This man shall be punished in the streets of the city, and where he suspecteth not he shall be taken.
text_marked: This man shall be punished in the streets of the city, and where he suspecteth not he shall be taken.

text: Thus shall it go also with the wife that leaveth her husband, and bringeth in an heir by another.
text_marked: Thus shall it go also with the wife that leaveth her husband, and bringeth in an heir by another.

text: For first, she hath disobeyed the law of the most High; and secondly, she hath trespassed against her own husband; and thirdly, she hath played the whore in adultery, and brought children by another man.
text_marked: For first, she hath disobeyed the law of the most High; and secondly, she hath trespassed against her own husband; and thirdly, she hath played the whore in adultery, and brought children by another man.

text: She shall be brought out into the congregation, and inquisition shall be made of her children.
text_marked: She shall be brought out into the congregation, and inquisition shall be made of her children.

text: Her children shall not take root, and her branches shall bring forth no fruit.
text_marked: Her children shall not take root, and her branches shall bring forth no fruit.

text: She shall leave her memory to be cursed, and her reproach shall not be blotted out.
text_marked: She shall leave her memory to be cursed, and her reproach shall not be blotted out.

text: And they that remain shall know that there is nothing better than the fear of the Lord, and that there is nothing sweeter than to take heed unto the commandments of the Lord.
text_marked: And they that remain shall know that there is nothing better than the fear of the Lord, and that there is nothing sweeter than to take heed unto the commandments of the Lord.

text: It is great glory to follow the Lord, and to be received of him is long life.
text_marked: It is great glory to follow the Lord, and to be received of him is long life.

text: Wisdom shall praise herself, and shall glory in the midst of her people.
text_marked: Wisdom shall praise herself, and shall glory in the midst of her people.

text: In the congregation of the most High shall she open her mouth, and triumph before his power.
text_marked: In the congregation of the most High shall she open her mouth, and triumph before his power.

text: I came out of the mouth of the most High, and covered the earth as a cloud.
text_marked: I came out of the mouth of the most High, and covered the earth as a cloud.

text: I dwelt in high places, and my throne is in a cloudy pillar.
text_marked: I dwelt in high places, and my throne is in a cloudy pillar.

text: I alone compassed the circuit of heaven, and walked in the bottom of the deep.
text_marked: I alone compassed the circuit of heaven, and walked in the bottom of the deep.

text: In the waves of the sea and in all the earth, and in every people and nation, I got a possession.
text_marked: In the waves of the sea and in all the earth, and in every people and nation, I got a possession.

text: With all these I sought rest: and in whose inheritance shall I abide?
text_marked: With all these I sought rest: and in whose inheritance shall I abide?

text: So the Creator of all things gave me a commandment, and he that made me caused my tabernacle to rest, and said, Let thy dwelling be in Jacob, and thine inheritance in Israel.
text_marked: So the Creator of all things gave me a commandment, and he that made me caused my tabernacle to rest, and said, Let thy dwelling be in Jacob, and thine inheritance in Israel.

text: He created me from the beginning before the world, and I shall never fail.
text_marked: He created me from the beginning before the world, and I shall never fail.

text: In the holy tabernacle I served before him; and so was I established in Sion.
text_marked: In the holy tabernacle I served before him; and so was I established in Sion.

text: Likewise in the beloved city he gave me rest, and in Jerusalem was my power.
text_marked: Likewise in the beloved city he gave me rest, and in Jerusalem was my power.

text: And I took root in an honourable people, even in the portion of the Lord’s inheritance.
text_marked: And I took root in an honourable people, even in the portion of the Lord’s inheritance.

text: I was exalted like a cedar in Libanus, and as a cypress tree upon the mountains of Hermon.
text_marked: I was exalted like a cedar in Libanus, and as a cypress tree upon the mountains of Hermon.

text: I was exalted like a palm tree in En-gaddi, and as a rose plant in Jericho, as a fair olive tree in a pleasant field, and grew up as a plane tree by the water.
text_marked: I was exalted like a palm tree in En-gaddi, and as a rose plant in Jericho, as a fair olive tree in a pleasant field, and grew up as a plane tree by the water.

text: I gave a sweet smell like cinnamon and aspalathus, and I yielded a pleasant odour like the best myrrh, as galbanum, and onyx, and sweet storax, and as the fume of frankincense in the tabernacle.
text_marked: I gave a sweet smell like cinnamon and aspalathus, and I yielded a pleasant odour like the best myrrh, as galbanum, and onyx, and sweet storax, and as the fume of frankincense in the tabernacle.

text: As the turpentine tree I stretched out my branches, and my branches are the branches of honour and grace.
text_marked: As the turpentine tree I stretched out my branches, and my branches are the branches of honour and grace.

text: As the vine brought I forth pleasant savour, and my flowers are the fruit of honour and riches.
text_marked: As the vine brought I forth pleasant savour, and my flowers are the fruit of honour and riches.

text: I am the mother of fair love, and fear, and knowledge, and holy hope: I therefore, being eternal, am given to all my children which are named of him.
text_marked: I am the mother of fair love, and fear, and knowledge, and holy hope: I therefore, being eternal, am given to all my children which are named of him.

text: Come unto me, all ye that be desirous of me, and fill yourselves with my fruits.
text_marked: Come unto me, all ye that be desirous of me, and fill yourselves with my fruits.

text: For my memorial is sweeter than honey, and mine inheritance than the honeycomb.
text_marked: For my memorial is sweeter than honey, and mine inheritance than the honeycomb.

text: They that eat me shall yet be hungry, and they that drink me shall yet be thirsty.
text_marked: They that eat me shall yet be hungry, and they that drink me shall yet be thirsty.

text: He that obeyeth me shall never be confounded, and they that work by me shall not do amiss.
text_marked: He that obeyeth me shall never be confounded, and they that work by me shall not do amiss.

text: All these things are the book of the covenant of the most high God, even the law which Moses commanded for an heritage unto the congregations of Jacob.
text_marked: All these things are the book of the covenant of the most high God, even the law which Moses commanded for an heritage unto the congregations of Jacob.

text: Faint not to be strong in the Lord; that he may confirm you, cleave unto him: for the Lord Almighty is God alone, and beside him there is no other Saviour.
text_marked: Faint not to be strong in the Lord; that he may confirm you, cleave unto him: for the Lord Almighty is God alone, and beside him there is no other Saviour.

text: He filleth all things with his wisdom, as Phison and as Tigris in the time of the new fruits.
text_marked: He filleth all things with his wisdom, as Phison and as Tigris in the time of the new fruits.

text: He maketh the understanding to abound like Euphrates, and as Jordan in the time of the harvest.
text_marked: He maketh the understanding to abound like Euphrates, and as Jordan in the time of the harvest.

text: He maketh the doctrine of knowledge appear as the light, and as Geon in the time of vintage.
text_marked: He maketh the doctrine of knowledge appear as the light, and as Geon in the time of vintage.

text: The first man knew her not perfectly: no more shall the last find her out.
text_marked: The first man knew her not perfectly: no more shall the last find her out.

text: For her thoughts are more than the sea, and her counsels profounder than the great deep.
text_marked: For her thoughts are more than the sea, and her counsels profounder than the great deep.

text: I also came out as a brook from a river, and as a conduit into a garden.
text_marked: I also came out as a brook from a river, and as a conduit into a garden.

text: I said, I will water my best garden, and will water abundantly my garden bed: and, lo, my brook became a river, and my river became a sea.
text_marked: I said, I will water my best garden, and will water abundantly my garden bed: and, lo, my brook became a river, and my river became a sea.

text: I will yet make doctrine to shine as the morning, and will send forth her light afar off.
text_marked: I will yet make doctrine to shine as the morning, and will send forth her light afar off.

text: I will yet pour out doctrine as prophecy, and leave it to all ages for ever.
text_marked: I will yet pour out doctrine as prophecy, and leave it to all ages for ever.

text: Behold that I have not laboured for myself only, but for all them that seek wisdom.
text_marked: Behold that I have not laboured for myself only, but for all them that seek wisdom.

text: In three things I was beautified, and stood up beautiful both before God and men: the unity of brethren, the love of neighbours, a man and a wife that agree together.
text_marked: In three things I was beautified, and stood up beautiful both before God and men: the unity of brethren, the love of neighbours, a man and a wife that agree together.

text: Three sorts of men my soul hateth, and I am greatly offended at their life: a poor man that is proud, a rich man that is a liar, and an old adulterer that doateth.
text_marked: Three sorts of men my soul hateth, and I am greatly offended at their life: a poor man that is proud, a rich man that is a liar, and an old adulterer that doateth.

text: If thou hast gathered nothing in thy youth, how canst thou find any thing in thine age?
text_marked: If thou hast gathered nothing in thy youth, how canst thou find any thing in thine age?

text: O how comely a thing is judgment for gray hairs, and for ancient men to know counsel!
text_marked: O how comely a thing is judgment for gray hairs, and for ancient men to know counsel!

text: O how comely is the wisdom of old men, and understanding and counsel to men of honour.
text_marked: O how comely is the wisdom of old men, and understanding and counsel to men of honour.

text: Much experience is the crown of old men, and the fear of God is their glory.
text_marked: Much experience is the crown of old men, and the fear of God is their glory.

text: There be nine things which I have judged in mine heart to be happy, and the tenth I will utter with my tongue: A man that hath joy of his children; and he that liveth to see the fall of his enemy:
text_marked: There be nine things which I have judged in mine heart to be happy, and the tenth I will utter with my tongue: A man that hath joy of his children; and he that liveth to see the fall of his enemy:

text: Well is him that dwelleth with a wife of understanding, and that hath not slipped with his tongue, and that hath not served a man more unworthy than himself:
text_marked: Well is him that dwelleth with a wife of understanding, and that hath not slipped with his tongue, and that hath not served a man more unworthy than himself:

text: Well is him that hath found prudence, and he that speaketh in the ears of them that will hear:
text_marked: Well is him that hath found prudence, and he that speaketh in the ears of them that will hear:

text: O how great is he that findeth wisdom! yet is there none above him that feareth the Lord.
text_marked: O how great is he that findeth wisdom! yet is there none above him that feareth the Lord.

text: But the love of the Lord passeth all things for illumination: he that holdeth it, whereto shall he be likened?
text_marked: But the love of the Lord passeth all things for illumination: he that holdeth it, whereto shall he be likened?

text: The fear of the Lord is the beginning of his love: and faith is the beginning of cleaving unto him.
text_marked: The fear of the Lord is the beginning of his love: and faith is the beginning of cleaving unto him.

text: Give me any plague, but the plague of the heart: and any wickedness, but the wickedness of a woman:
text_marked: [Give me] any plague, but the plague of the heart: and any wickedness, but the wickedness of a woman:

text: And any affliction, but the affliction from them that hate me: and any revenge, but the revenge of enemies.
text_marked: And any affliction, but the affliction from them that hate me: and any revenge, but the revenge of enemies.

text: There is no head above the head of a serpent; and there is no wrath above the wrath of an enemy.
text_marked: There is no head above the head of a serpent; and there is no wrath above the wrath of an enemy.

text: I had rather dwell with a lion and a dragon, than to keep house with a wicked woman.
text_marked: I had rather dwell with a lion and a dragon, than to keep house with a wicked woman.

text: The wickedness of a woman changeth her face, and darkeneth her countenance like sackcloth.
text_marked: The wickedness of a woman changeth her face, and darkeneth her countenance like sackcloth.

text: Her husband shall sit among his neighbours; and when he heareth it shall sigh bitterly.
text_marked: Her husband shall sit among his neighbours; and when he heareth it shall sigh bitterly.

text: All wickedness is but little to the wickedness of a woman: let the portion of a sinner fall upon her.
text_marked: All wickedness is but little to the wickedness of a woman: let the portion of a sinner fall upon her.

text: As the climbing up a sandy way is to the feet of the aged, so is a wife full of words to a quiet man.
text_marked: As the climbing up a sandy way is to the feet of the aged, so is a wife full of words to a quiet man.

text: Stumble not at the beauty of a woman, and desire her not for pleasure.
text_marked: Stumble not at the beauty of a woman, and desire her not for pleasure.

text: A woman, if she maintain her husband, is full of anger, impudence, and much reproach.
text_marked: A woman, if she maintain her husband, is full of anger, impudence, and much reproach.

text: A wicked woman abateth the courage, maketh an heavy countenance and a wounded heart: a woman that will not comfort her husband in distress maketh weak hands and feeble knees.
text_marked: A wicked woman abateth the courage, maketh an heavy countenance and a wounded heart: a woman that will not comfort her husband in distress maketh weak hands and feeble knees.

text: Of the woman came the beginning of sin, and through her we all die.
text_marked: Of the woman came the beginning of sin, and through her we all die.

text: Give the water no passage; neither a wicked woman liberty to gad abroad.
text_marked: Give the water no passage; neither a wicked woman liberty to gad abroad.

text: If she go not as thou wouldest have her, cut her off from thy flesh, and give her a bill of divorce, and let her go.
text_marked: If she go not as thou wouldest have her, cut her off from thy flesh, and give her a bill of divorce, and let her go.

text: Blessed is the man that hath a virtuous wife, for the number of his days shall be double.
text_marked: Blessed is the man that hath a virtuous wife, for the number of his days shall be double.

text: A virtuous woman rejoiceth her husband, and he shall fulfil the years of his life in peace.
text_marked: A virtuous woman rejoiceth her husband, and he shall fulfil the years of his life in peace.

text: A good wife is a good portion, which shall be given in the portion of them that fear the Lord.
text_marked: A good wife is a good portion, which shall be given in the portion of them that fear the Lord.

text: Whether a man be rich or poor, if he have a good heart toward the Lord, he shall at all times rejoice with a cheerful countenance.
text_marked: Whether a man be rich or poor, if he have a good heart toward the Lord, he shall at all times rejoice with a cheerful countenance.

text: There be three things that mine heart feareth; and for the fourth I was sore afraid: the slander of a city, the gathering together of an unruly multitude, and a false accusation: all these are worse than death.
text_marked: There be three things that mine heart feareth; and for the fourth I was sore afraid: the slander of a city, the gathering together of an unruly multitude, and a false accusation: all these are worse than death.

text: But a grief of heart and sorrow is a woman that is jealous over another woman, and a scourge of the tongue which communicateth with all.
text_marked: But a grief of heart and sorrow is a woman that is jealous over another woman, and a scourge of the tongue which communicateth with all.

text: An evil wife is a yoke shaken to and fro: he that hath hold of her is as though he held a scorpion.
text_marked: An evil wife is a yoke shaken to and fro: he that hath hold of her is as though he held a scorpion.

text: A drunken woman and a gadder abroad causeth great anger, and she will not cover her own shame.
text_marked: A drunken woman and a gadder abroad causeth great anger, and she will not cover her own shame.

text: The whoredom of a woman may be known in her haughty looks and eyelids.
text_marked: The whoredom of a woman may be known in her haughty looks and eyelids.

text: If thy daughter be shameless, keep her in straitly, lest she abuse herself through overmuch liberty.
text_marked: If thy daughter be shameless, keep her in straitly, lest she abuse herself through overmuch liberty.

text: Watch over an impudent eye: and marvel not if she trespass against thee.
text_marked: Watch over an impudent eye: and marvel not if she trespass against thee.

text: She will open her mouth, as a thirsty traveller when he hath found a fountain, and drink of every water near her: by every hedge will she sit down, and open her quiver against every arrow.
text_marked: She will open her mouth, as a thirsty traveller when he hath found a fountain, and drink of every water near her: by every hedge will she sit down, and open her quiver against every arrow.

text: The grace of a wife delighteth her husband, and her discretion will fatten his bones.
text_marked: The grace of a wife delighteth her husband, and her discretion will fatten his bones.

text: A silent and loving woman is a gift of the Lord; and there is nothing so much worth as a mind well instructed.
text_marked: A silent and loving woman is a gift of the Lord; and there is nothing so much worth as a mind well instructed.

text: A shamefaced and faithful woman is a double grace, and her continent mind cannot be valued.
text_marked: A shamefaced and faithful woman is a double grace, and her continent mind cannot be valued.

text: As the sun when it ariseth in the high heaven; so is the beauty of a good wife in the ordering of her house.
text_marked: As the sun when it ariseth in the high heaven; so is the beauty of a good wife in the ordering of her house.

text: As the clear light is upon the holy candlestick; so is the beauty of the face in ripe age.
text_marked: As the clear light is upon the holy candlestick; so is the beauty of the face in ripe age.

text: As the golden pillars are upon the sockets of silver; so are the fair feet with a constant heart.
text_marked: As the golden pillars are upon the sockets of silver; so are the fair feet with a constant heart.

text: My son, keep the flower of thine age sound; and give not thy strength to strangers.
text_marked: My son, keep the flower of thine age sound; and give not thy strength to strangers.

text: When thou hast gotten a fruitful possession through all the field, sow it with thine own seed, trusting in the goodness of thy stock.
text_marked: When thou hast gotten a fruitful possession through all the field, sow it with thine own seed, trusting in the goodness of thy stock.

text: So thy race which thou leavest shall be magnified, having the confidence of their good descent.
text_marked: So thy race which thou leavest shall be magnified, having the confidence of their good descent.

text: An harlot shall be accounted as spittle; but a married woman is a tower against death to her husband.
text_marked: An harlot shall be accounted as spittle; but a married woman is a tower against death to her husband.

text: A wicked woman is given as a portion to a wicked man: but a godly woman is given to him that feareth the Lord.
text_marked: A wicked woman is given as a portion to a wicked man: but a godly woman is given to him that feareth the Lord.

text: A dishonest woman contemneth shame: but an honest woman will reverence her husband.
text_marked: A dishonest woman contemneth shame: but an honest woman will reverence her husband.

text: A shameless woman shall be counted as a dog; but she that is shamefaced will fear the Lord.
text_marked: A shameless woman shall be counted as a dog; but she that is shamefaced will fear the Lord.

text: A woman that honoureth her husband shall be judged wise of all; but she that dishonoureth him in her pride shall be counted ungodly of all.
text_marked: A woman that honoureth her husband shall be judged wise of all; but she that dishonoureth him in her pride shall be counted ungodly of all.

text: A loud crying woman and a scold shall be sought out to drive away the enemies.
text_marked: A loud crying woman and a scold shall be sought out to drive away the enemies.

text: There be two things that grieve my heart; and the third maketh me angry: a man of war that suffereth poverty; and men of understanding that are not set by; and one that returneth from righteousness to sin; the Lord prepareth such an one for the sword.
text_marked: There be two things that grieve my heart; and the third maketh me angry: a man of war that suffereth poverty; and men of understanding that are not set by; and one that returneth from righteousness to sin; the Lord prepareth such an one for the sword.

text: A merchant shall hardly keep himself from doing wrong; and an huckster shall not be freed from sin.
text_marked: A merchant shall hardly keep himself from doing wrong; and an huckster shall not be freed from sin.

text: Many have sinned for a small matter; and he that seeketh for abundance will turn his eyes away.
text_marked: Many have sinned for a small matter; and he that seeketh for abundance will turn his eyes away.

text: As a nail sticketh fast between the joinings of the stones; so doth sin stick close between buying and selling.
text_marked: As a nail sticketh fast between the joinings of the stones; so doth sin stick close between buying and selling.

text: Unless a man hold himself diligently in the fear of the Lord, his house shall soon be overthrown.
text_marked: Unless a man hold himself diligently in the fear of the Lord, his house shall soon be overthrown.

text: As when one sifteth with a sieve, the refuse remaineth; so the filth of man in his talk.
text_marked: As when one sifteth with a sieve, the refuse remaineth; so the filth of man in his talk.

text: The furnace proveth the potter’s vessels; so the trial of man is in his reasoning.
text_marked: The furnace proveth the potter’s vessels; so the trial of man is in his reasoning.

text: The fruit declareth if the tree have been dressed; so is the utterance of a conceit in the heart of man.
text_marked: The fruit declareth if the tree have been dressed; so is the utterance of a conceit in the heart of man.

text: Praise no man before thou hearest him speak; for this is the trial of men.
text_marked: Praise no man before thou hearest him speak; for this is the trial of men.

text: If thou followest righteousness, thou shalt obtain her, and put her on, as a glorious long robe.
text_marked: If thou followest righteousness, thou shalt obtain her, and put her on, as a glorious long robe.

text: The birds will resort unto their like; so will truth return unto them that practise in her.
text_marked: The birds will resort unto their like; so will truth return unto them that practise in her.

text: As the lion lieth in wait for the prey; so sin for them that work iniquity.
text_marked: As the lion lieth in wait for the prey; so sin for them that work iniquity.

text: The discourse of a godly man is always with wisdom; but a fool changeth as the moon.
text_marked: The discourse of a godly man is always with wisdom; but a fool changeth as the moon.

text: If thou be among the indiscreet, observe the time; but be continually among men of understanding.
text_marked: If thou be among the indiscreet, observe the time; but be continually among men of understanding.

text: The discourse of fools is irksome, and their sport is the wantonness of sin.
text_marked: The discourse of fools is irksome, and their sport is the wantonness of sin.

text: The talk of him that sweareth much maketh the hair stand upright; and their brawls make one stop his ears.
text_marked: The talk of him that sweareth much maketh the hair stand upright; and their brawls make one stop his ears.

text: The strife of the proud is bloodshedding, and their revilings are grievous to the ear.
text_marked: The strife of the proud is bloodshedding, and their revilings are grievous to the ear.

text: Whoso discovereth secrets loseth his credit; and shall never find friend to his mind.
text_marked: Whoso discovereth secrets loseth his credit; and shall never find friend to his mind.

text: Love thy friend, and be faithful unto him: but if thou betrayest his secrets, follow no more after him.
text_marked: Love thy friend, and be faithful unto him: but if thou betrayest his secrets, follow no more after him.

text: For as a man hath destroyed his enemy; so hast thou lost the love of thy neighbor.
text_marked: For as a man hath destroyed his enemy; so hast thou lost the love of thy neighbor.

text: As one that letteth a bird go out of his hand, so hast thou let thy neighbour go, and shalt not get him again
text_marked: As one that letteth a bird go out of his hand, so hast thou let thy neighbour go, and shalt not get him again

text: Follow after him no more, for he is too far off; he is as a roe escaped out of the snare.
text_marked: Follow after him no more, for he is too far off; he is as a roe escaped out of the snare.

text: As for a wound, it may be bound up; and after reviling there may be reconcilement: but he that betrayeth secrets is without hope.
text_marked: As for a wound, it may be bound up; and after reviling there may be reconcilement: but he that betrayeth secrets is without hope.

text: He that winketh with the eyes worketh evil: and he that knoweth him will depart from him.
text_marked: He that winketh with the eyes worketh evil: and he that knoweth him will depart from him.

text: When thou art present, he will speak sweetly, and will admire thy words: but at the last he will writhe his mouth, and slander thy sayings.
text_marked: When thou art present, he will speak sweetly, and will admire thy words: but at the last he will writhe his mouth, and slander thy sayings.

text: I have hated many things, but nothing like him; for the Lord will hate him.
text_marked: I have hated many things, but nothing like him; for the Lord will hate him.

text: Whoso casteth a stone on high casteth it on his own head; and a deceitful stroke shall make wounds.
text_marked: Whoso casteth a stone on high casteth it on his own head; and a deceitful stroke shall make wounds.

text: Whoso diggeth a pit shall fall therein: and he that setteth a trap shall be taken therein.
text_marked: Whoso diggeth a pit shall fall therein: and he that setteth a trap shall be taken therein.

text: He that worketh mischief, it shall fall upon him, and he shall not know whence it cometh.
text_marked: He that worketh mischief, it shall fall upon him, and he shall not know whence it cometh.

text: Mockery and reproach are from the proud; but vengeance, as a lion, shall lie in wait for them.
text_marked: Mockery and reproach are from the proud; but vengeance, as a lion, shall lie in wait for them.

text: They that rejoice at the fall of the righteous shall be taken in the snare; and anguish shall consume them before they die.
text_marked: They that rejoice at the fall of the righteous shall be taken in the snare; and anguish shall consume them before they die.

text: Malice and wrath, even these are abominations; and the sinful man shall have them both.
text_marked: Malice and wrath, even these are abominations; and the sinful man shall have them both.

text: He that revengeth shall find vengeance from the Lord, and he will surely keep his sins in remembrance.
text_marked: He that revengeth shall find vengeance from the Lord, and he will surely keep his sins [in remembrance].

text: Forgive thy neighbour the hurt that he hath done unto thee, so shall thy sins also be forgiven when thou prayest.
text_marked: Forgive thy neighbour the hurt that he hath done unto thee, so shall thy sins also be forgiven when thou prayest.

text: One man beareth hatred against another, and doth he seek pardon from the Lord?
text_marked: One man beareth hatred against another, and doth he seek pardon from the Lord?

text: He sheweth no mercy to a man, which is like himself: and doth he ask forgiveness of his own sins?
text_marked: He sheweth no mercy to a man, which is like himself: and doth he ask forgiveness of his own sins?

text: If he that is but flesh nourish hatred, who will intreat for pardon of his sins?
text_marked: If he that is but flesh nourish hatred, who will intreat for pardon of his sins?

text: Remember thy end, and let enmity cease; remember corruption and death, and abide in the commandments.
text_marked: Remember thy end, and let enmity cease; [remember] corruption and death, and abide in the commandments.

text: Remember the commandments, and bear no malice to thy neighbour: remember the covenant of the Highest, and wink at ignorance.
text_marked: Remember the commandments, and bear no malice to thy neighbour: [remember] the covenant of the Highest, and wink at ignorance.

text: Abstain from strife, and thou shalt diminish thy sins: for a furious man will kindle strife,
text_marked: Abstain from strife, and thou shalt diminish thy sins: for a furious man will kindle strife,

text: A sinful man disquieteth friends, and maketh debate among them that be at peace.
text_marked: A sinful man disquieteth friends, and maketh debate among them that be at peace.

text: As the matter of the fire is, so it burneth: and as a man’s strength is, so is his wrath; and according to his riches his anger riseth; and the stronger they are which contend, the more they will be inflamed.
text_marked: As the matter of the fire is, so it burneth: and as a man’s strength is, so is his wrath; and according to his riches his anger riseth; and the stronger they are which contend, the more they will be inflamed.

text: An hasty contention kindleth a fire: and an hasty fighting sheddeth blood.
text_marked: An hasty contention kindleth a fire: and an hasty fighting sheddeth blood.

text: If thou blow the spark, it shall burn: if thou spit upon it, it shall be quenched: and both these come out of thy mouth.
