text_marked: But every man followed the imagination of his own wicked heart, to serve strange gods, and to do evil in the sight of the Lord our God.

text: Therefore the Lord hath made good his word, which he pronounced against us, and against our judges that judged Israel, and against our kings, and against our princes, and against the men of Israel and Juda,
text_marked: Therefore the Lord hath made good his word, which he pronounced against us, and against our judges that judged Israel, and against our kings, and against our princes, and against the men of Israel and Juda,

text: To bring upon us great plagues, such as never happened under the whole heaven, as it came to pass in Jerusalem, according to the things that were written in the law of Moses;
text_marked: To bring upon us great plagues, such as never happened under the whole heaven, as it came to pass in Jerusalem, according to the things that were written in the law of Moses;

text: That a man should eat the flesh of his own son, and the flesh of his own daughter.
text_marked: That a man should eat the flesh of his own son, and the flesh of his own daughter.

text: Moreover he hath delivered them to be in subjection to all the kingdoms that are round about us, to be as a reproach and desolation among all the people round about, where the Lord hath scattered them.
text_marked: Moreover he hath delivered them to be in subjection to all the kingdoms that are round about us, to be as a reproach and desolation among all the people round about, where the Lord hath scattered them.

text: Thus we were cast down, and not exalted, because we have sinned against the Lord our God, and have not been obedient unto his voice.
text_marked: Thus we were cast down, and not exalted, because we have sinned against the Lord our God, and have not been obedient unto his voice.

text: To the Lord our God appertaineth righteousness: but unto us and to our fathers open shame, as appeareth this day.
text_marked: To the Lord our God appertaineth righteousness: but unto us and to our fathers open shame, as appeareth this day.

text: For all these plagues are come upon us, which the Lord hath pronounced against us
text_marked: For all these plagues are come upon us, which the Lord hath pronounced against us

text: Yet have we not prayed before the Lord, that we might turn every one from the imaginations of his wicked heart.
text_marked: Yet have we not prayed before the Lord, that we might turn every one from the imaginations of his wicked heart.

text: Wherefore the Lord watched over us for evil, and the Lord hath brought it upon us: for the Lord is righteous in all his works which he hath commanded us.
text_marked: Wherefore the Lord watched over us for evil, and the Lord hath brought it upon us: for the Lord is righteous in all his works which he hath commanded us.

text: Yet we have not hearkened unto his voice, to walk in the commandments of the Lord, that he hath set before us.
text_marked: Yet we have not hearkened unto his voice, to walk in the commandments of the Lord, that he hath set before us.

text: And now, O Lord God of Israel, that hast brought thy people out of the land of Egypt with a mighty hand, and high arm, and with signs, and with wonders, and with great power, and hast gotten thyself a name, as appeareth this day:
text_marked: And now, O Lord God of Israel, that hast brought thy people out of the land of Egypt with a mighty hand, and high arm, and with signs, and with wonders, and with great power, and hast gotten thyself a name, as appeareth this day:

text: O Lord our God, we have sinned, we have done ungodly, we have dealt unrighteously in all thine ordinances.
text_marked: O Lord our God, we have sinned, we have done ungodly, we have dealt unrighteously in all thine ordinances.

text: Let thy wrath turn from us: for we are but a few left among the heathen, where thou hast scattered us.
text_marked: Let thy wrath turn from us: for we are but a few left among the heathen, where thou hast scattered us.

text: Hear our prayers, O Lord, and our petitions, and deliver us for thine own sake, and give us favour in the sight of them which have led us away:
text_marked: Hear our prayers, O Lord, and our petitions, and deliver us for thine own sake, and give us favour in the sight of them which have led us away:

text: That all the earth may know that thou art the Lord our God, because Israel and his posterity is called by thy name.
text_marked: That all the earth may know that thou art the Lord our God, because Israel and his posterity is called by thy name.

text: O Lord, look down from thine holy house, and consider us: bow down thine ear, O Lord, to hear us.
text_marked: O Lord, look down from thine holy house, and consider us: bow down thine ear, O Lord, to hear us.

text: Open thine eyes, and behold; for the dead that are in the graves, whose souls are taken from their bodies, will give unto the Lord neither praise nor righteousness:
text_marked: Open thine eyes, and behold; for the dead that are in the graves, whose souls are taken from their bodies, will give unto the Lord neither praise nor righteousness:

text: But the soul that is greatly vexed, which goeth stooping and feeble, and the eyes that fail, and the hungry soul, will give thee praise and righteousness, O Lord.
text_marked: But the soul that is greatly vexed, which goeth stooping and feeble, and the eyes that fail, and the hungry soul, will give thee praise and righteousness, O Lord.

text: Therefore we do not make our humble supplication before thee, O Lord our God, for the righteousness of our fathers, and of our kings.
text_marked: Therefore we do not make our humble supplication before thee, O Lord our God, for the righteousness of our fathers, and of our kings.

text: For thou hast sent out thy wrath and indignation upon us, as thou hast spoken by thy servants the prophets, saying,
text_marked: For thou hast sent out thy wrath and indignation upon us, as thou hast spoken by thy servants the prophets, saying,

text: Thus saith the Lord, Bow down your shoulders to serve the king of Babylon: so shall ye remain in the land that I gave unto your fathers.
text_marked: Thus saith the Lord, Bow down your shoulders to serve the king of Babylon: so shall ye remain in the land that I gave unto your fathers.

text: But if ye will not hear the voice of the Lord, to serve the king of Babylon,
text_marked: But if ye will not hear the voice of the Lord, to serve the king of Babylon,

text: I will cause to cease out of the cites of Judah, and from without Jerusalem, the voice of mirth, and the voice of joy, the voice of the bridegroom, and the voice of the bride: and the whole land shall be desolate of inhabitants.
text_marked: I will cause to cease out of the cites of Judah, and from without Jerusalem, the voice of mirth, and the voice of joy, the voice of the bridegroom, and the voice of the bride: and the whole land shall be desolate of inhabitants.

text: But we would not hearken unto thy voice, to serve the king of Babylon: therefore hast thou made good the words that thou spakest by thy servants the prophets, namely, that the bones of our kings, and the bones of our fathers, should be taken out of their place.
text_marked: But we would not hearken unto thy voice, to serve the king of Babylon: therefore hast thou made good the words that thou spakest by thy servants the prophets, namely, that the bones of our kings, and the bones of our fathers, should be taken out of their place.

text: And, lo, they are cast out to the heat of the day, and to the frost of the night, and they died in great miseries by famine, by sword, and by pestilence.
text_marked: And, lo, they are cast out to the heat of the day, and to the frost of the night, and they died in great miseries by famine, by sword, and by pestilence.

text: And the house which is called by thy name hast thou laid waste, as it is to be seen this day, for the wickedness of the house of Israel and the house of Juda.
text_marked: And the house which is called by thy name hast thou laid waste, as it is to be seen this day, for the wickedness of the house of Israel and the house of Juda.

text: O Lord our God, thou hast dealt with us after all thy goodness, and according to all that great mercy of thine,
text_marked: O Lord our God, thou hast dealt with us after all thy goodness, and according to all that great mercy of thine,

text: As thou spakest by thy servant Moses in the day when thou didst command him to write the law before the children of Israel, saying,
text_marked: As thou spakest by thy servant Moses in the day when thou didst command him to write the law before the children of Israel, saying,

text: If ye will not hear my voice, surely this very great multitude shall be turned into a small number among the nations, where I will scatter them.
text_marked: If ye will not hear my voice, surely this very great multitude shall be turned into a small number among the nations, where I will scatter them.

text: For I knew that they would not hear me, because it is a stiffnecked people: but in the land of their captivities they shall remember themselves.
text_marked: For I knew that they would not hear me, because it is a stiffnecked people: but in the land of their captivities they shall remember themselves.

text: And shall know that I am the Lord their God: for I will give them an heart, and ears to hear:
text_marked: And shall know that I am the Lord their God: for I will give them an heart, and ears to hear:

text: And they shall praise me in the land of their captivity, and think upon my name,
text_marked: And they shall praise me in the land of their captivity, and think upon my name,

text: And return from their stiff neck, and from their wicked deeds: for they shall remember the way of their fathers, which sinned before the Lord.
text_marked: And return from their stiff neck, and from their wicked deeds: for they shall remember the way of their fathers, which sinned before the Lord.

text: And I will bring them again into the land which I promised with an oath unto their fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and they shall be lords of it: and I will increase them, and they shall not be diminished.
text_marked: And I will bring them again into the land which I promised with an oath unto their fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and they shall be lords of it: and I will increase them, and they shall not be diminished.

text: And I will make an everlasting covenant with them to be their God, and they shall be my people: and I will no more drive my people of Israel out of the land that I have given them.
text_marked: And I will make an everlasting covenant with them to be their God, and they shall be my people: and I will no more drive my people of Israel out of the land that I have given them.

text: O Lord Almighty, God of Israel, the soul in anguish the troubled spirit, crieth unto thee.
text_marked: O Lord Almighty, God of Israel, the soul in anguish the troubled spirit, crieth unto thee.

text: Hear, O Lord, and have mercy; for thou art merciful: and have pity upon us, because we have sinned before thee.
text_marked: Hear, O Lord, and have mercy; for thou art merciful: and have pity upon us, because we have sinned before thee.

text: For thou endurest for ever, and we perish utterly.
text_marked: For thou endurest for ever, and we perish utterly.

text: O Lord Almighty, thou God of Israel, hear now the prayers of the dead Israelites, and of their children, which have sinned before thee, and not hearkened unto the voice of thee their God: for the which cause these plagues cleave unto us.
text_marked: O Lord Almighty, thou God of Israel, hear now the prayers of the dead Israelites, and of their children, which have sinned before thee, and not hearkened unto the voice of thee their God: for the which cause these plagues cleave unto us.

text: Remember not the iniquities of our forefathers: but think upon thy power and thy name now at this time.
text_marked: Remember not the iniquities of our forefathers: but think upon thy power and thy name now at this time.

text: For thou art the Lord our God, and thee, O Lord, will we praise.
text_marked: For thou art the Lord our God, and thee, O Lord, will we praise.

text: And for this cause thou hast put thy fear in our hearts, to the intent that we should call upon thy name, and praise thee in our captivity: for we have called to mind all the iniquity of our forefathers, that sinned before thee.
text_marked: And for this cause thou hast put thy fear in our hearts, to the intent that we should call upon thy name, and praise thee in our captivity: for we have called to mind all the iniquity of our forefathers, that sinned before thee.

text: Behold, we are yet this day in our captivity, where thou hast scattered us, for a reproach and a curse, and to be subject to payments, according to all the iniquities of our fathers, which departed from the Lord our God.
text_marked: Behold, we are yet this day in our captivity, where thou hast scattered us, for a reproach and a curse, and to be subject to payments, according to all the iniquities of our fathers, which departed from the Lord our God.

text: Hear, Israel, the commandments of life: give ear to understand wisdom.
text_marked: Hear, Israel, the commandments of life: give ear to understand wisdom.

text: How happeneth it Israel, that thou art in thine enemies’ land, that thou art waxen old in a strange country, that thou art defiled with the dead,
text_marked: How happeneth it Israel, that thou art in thine enemies’ land, that thou art waxen old in a strange country, that thou art defiled with the dead,

text: That thou art counted with them that go down into the grave?
text_marked: That thou art counted with them that go down into the grave?

text: Thou hast forsaken the fountain of wisdom.
text_marked: Thou hast forsaken the fountain of wisdom.

text: For if thou hadst walked in the way of God, thou shouldest have dwelled in peace for ever.
text_marked: For if thou hadst walked in the way of God, thou shouldest have dwelled in peace for ever.

text: Learn where is wisdom, where is strength, where is understanding; that thou mayest know also where is length of days, and life, where is the light of the eyes, and peace.
text_marked: Learn where is wisdom, where is strength, where is understanding; that thou mayest know also where is length of days, and life, where is the light of the eyes, and peace.

text: Who hath found out her place? or who hath come into her treasures?
text_marked: Who hath found out her place? or who hath come into her treasures?

text: Where are the princes of the heathen become, and such as ruled the beasts upon the earth;
text_marked: Where are the princes of the heathen become, and such as ruled the beasts upon the earth;

text: They that had their pastime with the fowls of the air, and they that hoarded up silver and gold, wherein men trust, and made no end of their getting?
text_marked: They that had their pastime with the fowls of the air, and they that hoarded up silver and gold, wherein men trust, and made no end of their getting?

text: For they that wrought in silver, and were so careful, and whose works are unsearchable,
text_marked: For they that wrought in silver, and were so careful, and whose works are unsearchable,

text: They are vanished and gone down to the grave, and others are come up in their steads.
text_marked: They are vanished and gone down to the grave, and others are come up in their steads.

text: Young men have seen light, and dwelt upon the earth: but the way of knowledge have they not known,
text_marked: Young men have seen light, and dwelt upon the earth: but the way of knowledge have they not known,

text: Nor understood the paths thereof, nor laid hold of it: their children were far off from that way.
text_marked: Nor understood the paths thereof, nor laid hold of it: their children were far off from that way.

text: It hath not been heard of in Chanaan, neither hath it been seen in Theman.
text_marked: It hath not been heard of in Chanaan, neither hath it been seen in Theman.

text: The Agarenes that seek wisdom upon earth, the merchants of Meran and of Theman, the authors of fables, and searchers out of understanding; none of these have known the way of wisdom, or remember her paths.
text_marked: The Agarenes that seek wisdom upon earth, the merchants of Meran and of Theman, the authors of fables, and searchers out of understanding; none of these have known the way of wisdom, or remember her paths.

text: O Israel, how great is the house of God! and how large is the place of his possession!
text_marked: O Israel, how great is the house of God! and how large is the place of his possession!

text: Great, and hath none end; high, and unmeasurable.
text_marked: Great, and hath none end; high, and unmeasurable.

text: There were the giants famous from the beginning, that were of so great stature, and so expert in war.
text_marked: There were the giants famous from the beginning, that were of so great stature, and so expert in war.

text: Those did not the Lord choose, neither gave he the way of knowledge unto them:
text_marked: Those did not the Lord choose, neither gave he the way of knowledge unto them:

text: But they were destroyed, because they had no wisdom, and perished through their own foolishness.
text_marked: But they were destroyed, because they had no wisdom, and perished through their own foolishness.

text: Who hath gone up into heaven, and taken her, and brought her down from the clouds?
text_marked: Who hath gone up into heaven, and taken her, and brought her down from the clouds?

text: Who hath gone over the sea, and found her, and will bring her for pure gold?
text_marked: Who hath gone over the sea, and found her, and will bring her for pure gold?

text: No man knoweth her way, nor thinketh of her path.
text_marked: No man knoweth her way, nor thinketh of her path.

text: But he that knoweth all things knoweth her, and hath found her out with his understanding: he that prepared the earth for evermore hath filled it with fourfooted beasts:
text_marked: But he that knoweth all things knoweth her, and hath found her out with his understanding: he that prepared the earth for evermore hath filled it with fourfooted beasts:

text: He that sendeth forth light, and it goeth, calleth it again, and it obeyeth him with fear.
text_marked: He that sendeth forth light, and it goeth, calleth it again, and it obeyeth him with fear.

text: The stars shined in their watches, and rejoiced: when he calleth them, they say, Here we be; and so with cheerfulness they shewed light unto him that made them.
text_marked: The stars shined in their watches, and rejoiced: when he calleth them, they say, Here we be; and so with cheerfulness they shewed light unto him that made them.

text: This is our God, and there shall none other be accounted of in comparison of him
text_marked: This is our God, and there shall none other be accounted of in comparison of him

text: He hath found out all the way of knowledge, and hath given it unto Jacob his servant, and to Israel his beloved.
text_marked: He hath found out all the way of knowledge, and hath given it unto Jacob his servant, and to Israel his beloved.

text: Afterward did he shew himself upon earth, and conversed with men.
text_marked: Afterward did he shew himself upon earth, and conversed with men.

text: This is the book of the commandments of God, and the law that endureth for ever: all they that keep it shall come to life; but such as leave it shall die.
text_marked: This is the book of the commandments of God, and the law that endureth for ever: all they that keep it shall come to life; but such as leave it shall die.

text: Turn thee, O Jacob, and take hold of it: walk in the presence of the light thereof, that thou mayest be illuminated.
text_marked: Turn thee, O Jacob, and take hold of it: walk in the presence of the light thereof, that thou mayest be illuminated.

text: Give not thine honour to another, nor the things that are profitable unto thee to a strange nation.
text_marked: Give not thine honour to another, nor the things that are profitable unto thee to a strange nation.

text: O Israel, happy are we: for things that are pleasing to God are made known unto us.
text_marked: O Israel, happy are we: for things that are pleasing to God are made known unto us.

text: Be of good cheer, my people, the memorial of Israel.
text_marked: Be of good cheer, my people, the memorial of Israel.

text: Ye were sold to the nations, not for your destruction: but because ye moved God to wrath, ye were delivered unto the enemies.
text_marked: Ye were sold to the nations, not for [your] destruction: but because ye moved God to wrath, ye were delivered unto the enemies.

text: For ye provoked him that made you by sacrificing unto devils, and not to God.
text_marked: For ye provoked him that made you by sacrificing unto devils, and not to God.

text: Ye have forgotten the everlasting God, that brought you up; and ye have grieved Jerusalem, that nursed you.
text_marked: Ye have forgotten the everlasting God, that brought you up; and ye have grieved Jerusalem, that nursed you.

text: For when she saw the wrath of God coming upon you, she said, Hearken, O ye that dwell about Sion: God hath brought upon me great mourning;
text_marked: For when she saw the wrath of God coming upon you, she said, Hearken, O ye that dwell about Sion: God hath brought upon me great mourning;

text: For I saw the captivity of my sons and daughters, which the Everlasting brought upon them.
text_marked: For I saw the captivity of my sons and daughters, which the Everlasting brought upon them.

text: With joy did I nourish them; but sent them away with weeping and mourning.
text_marked: With joy did I nourish them; but sent them away with weeping and mourning.

text: Let no man rejoice over me, a widow, and forsaken of many, who for the sins of my children am left desolate; because they departed from the law of God.
text_marked: Let no man rejoice over me, a widow, and forsaken of many, who for the sins of my children am left desolate; because they departed from the law of God.

text: They knew not his statutes, nor walked in the ways of his commandments, nor trod in the paths of discipline in his righteousness.
text_marked: They knew not his statutes, nor walked in the ways of his commandments, nor trod in the paths of discipline in his righteousness.

text: Let them that dwell about Sion come, and remember ye the captivity of my sons and daughters, which the Everlasting hath brought upon them.
text_marked: Let them that dwell about Sion come, and remember ye the captivity of my sons and daughters, which the Everlasting hath brought upon them.

text: For he hath brought a nation upon them from far, a shameless nation, and of a strange language, who neither reverenced old man, nor pitied child.
text_marked: For he hath brought a nation upon them from far, a shameless nation, and of a strange language, who neither reverenced old man, nor pitied child.

text: These have carried away the dear beloved children of the widow, and left her that was alone desolate without daughters.
text_marked: These have carried away the dear beloved children of the widow, and left her that was alone desolate without daughters.

text: But what can I help you?
text_marked: But what can I help you?

text: For he that brought these plagues upon you will deliver you from the hands of your enemies.
text_marked: For he that brought these plagues upon you will deliver you from the hands of your enemies.

text: Go your way, O my children, go your way: for I am left desolate.
text_marked: Go your way, O my children, go your way: for I am left desolate.

text: I have put off the clothing of peace, and put upon me the sackcloth of my prayer: I will cry unto the Everlasting in my days.
text_marked: I have put off the clothing of peace, and put upon me the sackcloth of my prayer: I will cry unto the Everlasting in my days.

text: Be of good cheer, O my children, cry unto the Lord, and he will deliver you from the power and hand of the enemies.
text_marked: Be of good cheer, O my children, cry unto the Lord, and he will deliver you from the power and hand of the enemies.

text: For my hope is in the Everlasting, that he will save you; and joy is come unto me from the Holy One, because of the mercy which shall soon come unto you from the Everlasting our Saviour.
text_marked: For my hope is in the Everlasting, that he will save you; and joy is come unto me from the Holy One, because of the mercy which shall soon come unto you from the Everlasting our Saviour.

text: For I sent you out with mourning and weeping: but God will give you to me again with joy and gladness for ever.
text_marked: For I sent you out with mourning and weeping: but God will give you to me again with joy and gladness for ever.

text: Like as now the neighbours of Sion have seen your captivity: so shall they see shortly your salvation from our God which shall come upon you with great glory, and brightness of the Everlasting.
text_marked: Like as now the neighbours of Sion have seen your captivity: so shall they see shortly your salvation from our God which shall come upon you with great glory, and brightness of the Everlasting.

text: My children, suffer patiently the wrath that is come upon you from God: for thine enemy hath persecuted thee; but shortly thou shalt see his destruction, and shalt tread upon his neck.
text_marked: My children, suffer patiently the wrath that is come upon you from God: for thine enemy hath persecuted thee; but shortly thou shalt see his destruction, and shalt tread upon his neck.

text: My delicate ones have gone rough ways, and were taken away as a flock caught of the enemies.
text_marked: My delicate ones have gone rough ways, and were taken away as a flock caught of the enemies.

text: Be of good comfort, O my children, and cry unto God: for ye shall be remembered of him that brought these things upon you.
text_marked: Be of good comfort, O my children, and cry unto God: for ye shall be remembered of him that brought these things upon you.

text: For as it was your mind to go astray from God: so, being returned, seek him ten times more.
text_marked: For as it was your mind to go astray from God: so, being returned, seek him ten times more.

text: For he that hath brought these plagues upon you shall bring you everlasting joy with your salvation.
text_marked: For he that hath brought these plagues upon you shall bring you everlasting joy with your salvation.

text: Take a good heart, O Jerusalem: for he that gave thee that name will comfort thee.
text_marked: Take a good heart, O Jerusalem: for he that gave thee that name will comfort thee.

text: Miserable are they that afflicted thee, and rejoiced at thy fall.
text_marked: Miserable are they that afflicted thee, and rejoiced at thy fall.

text: Miserable are the cities which thy children served: miserable is she that received thy sons.
text_marked: Miserable are the cities which thy children served: miserable is she that received thy sons.

text: For as she rejoiced at thy ruin, and was glad of thy fall: so shall she be grieved for her own desolation.
text_marked: For as she rejoiced at thy ruin, and was glad of thy fall: so shall she be grieved for her own desolation.

text: For I will take away the rejoicing of her great multitude, and her pride shall be turned into mourning.
text_marked: For I will take away the rejoicing of her great multitude, and her pride shall be turned into mourning.

text: For fire shall come upon her from the Everlasting, long to endure; and she shall be inhabited of devils for a great time.
text_marked: For fire shall come upon her from the Everlasting, long to endure; and she shall be inhabited of devils for a great time.

text: O Jerusalem, look about thee toward the east, and behold the joy that cometh unto thee from God.
text_marked: O Jerusalem, look about thee toward the east, and behold the joy that cometh unto thee from God.

text: Lo, thy sons come, whom thou sentest away, they come gathered together from the east to the west by the word of the Holy One, rejoicing in the glory of God.
text_marked: Lo, thy sons come, whom thou sentest away, they come gathered together from the east to the west by the word of the Holy One, rejoicing in the glory of God.

text: Put off, O Jerusalem, the garment of mourning and affliction, and put on the comeliness of the glory that cometh from God for ever.
text_marked: Put off, O Jerusalem, the garment of mourning and affliction, and put on the comeliness of the glory that cometh from God for ever.

text: Cast about thee a double garment of the righteousness which cometh from God; and set a diadem on thine head of the glory of the Everlasting.
text_marked: Cast about thee a double garment of the righteousness which cometh from God; and set a diadem on thine head of the glory of the Everlasting.

text: For God will shew thy brightness unto every country under heaven.
text_marked: For God will shew thy brightness unto every country under heaven.

text: For thy name shall be called of God for ever The peace of righteousness, and The glory of God’s worship.
text_marked: For thy name shall be called of God for ever The peace of righteousness, and The glory of God’s worship.

text: Arise, O Jerusalem, and stand on high, and look about toward the east, and behold thy children gathered from the west unto the east by the word of the Holy One, rejoicing in the remembrance of God.
text_marked: Arise, O Jerusalem, and stand on high, and look about toward the east, and behold thy children gathered from the west unto the east by the word of the Holy One, rejoicing in the remembrance of God.

text: For they departed from thee on foot, and were led away of their enemies: but God bringeth them unto thee exalted with glory, as children of the kingdom.
text_marked: For they departed from thee on foot, and were led away of their enemies: but God bringeth them unto thee exalted with glory, as children of the kingdom.

text: For God hath appointed that every high hill, and banks of long continuance, should be cast down, and valleys filled up, to make even the ground, that Israel may go safely in the glory of God,
text_marked: For God hath appointed that every high hill, and banks of long continuance, should be cast down, and valleys filled up, to make even the ground, that Israel may go safely in the glory of God,

text: Moreover even the woods and every sweetsmelling tree shall overshadow Israel by the commandment of God.
text_marked: Moreover even the woods and every sweetsmelling tree shall overshadow Israel by the commandment of God.

text: For God shall lead Israel with joy in the light of his glory with the mercy and righteousness that cometh from him.
text_marked: For God shall lead Israel with joy in the light of his glory with the mercy and righteousness that cometh from him.

text: A copy of an epistle, which Jeremy sent unto them which were to be led captives into Babylon by the king of the Babylonians, to certify them, as it was commanded him of God.
text_marked: A copy of an epistle, which Jeremy sent unto them which were to be led captives into Babylon by the king of the Babylonians, to certify them, as it was commanded him of God.

text: Because of the sins which ye have committed before God, ye shall be led away captives into Babylon by Nabuchodonosor king of the Babylonians.
text_marked: Because of the sins which ye have committed before God, ye shall be led away captives into Babylon by Nabuchodonosor king of the Babylonians.

text: So when ye be come unto Babylon, ye shall remain there many years, and for a long season, namely, seven generations: and after that I will bring you away peaceably from thence.
text_marked: So when ye be come unto Babylon, ye shall remain there many years, and for a long season, namely, seven generations: and after that I will bring you away peaceably from thence.

text: Now shall ye see in Babylon gods of silver, and of gold, and of wood, borne upon shoulders, which cause the nations to fear.
text_marked: Now shall ye see in Babylon gods of silver, and of gold, and of wood, borne upon shoulders, which cause the nations to fear.

text: Beware therefore that ye in no wise be like to strangers, neither be ye afraid of them, when ye see the multitude before them and behind them, worshipping them.
text_marked: Beware therefore that ye in no wise be like to strangers, neither be ye afraid of them, when ye see the multitude before them and behind them, worshipping them.

text: But say ye in your hearts, O Lord, we must worship thee.
text_marked: But say ye in your hearts, O Lord, we must worship thee.

text: For mine angel is with you, and I myself caring for your souls.
text_marked: For mine angel is with you, and I myself caring for your souls.

text: As for their tongue, it is polished by the workman, and they themselves are gilded and laid over with silver; yet are they but false, and cannot speak.
text_marked: As for their tongue, it is polished by the workman, and they themselves are gilded and laid over with silver; yet are they but false, and cannot speak.

text: And taking gold, as it were for a virgin that loveth to go gay, they make crowns for the heads of their gods.
text_marked: And taking gold, as it were for a virgin that loveth to go gay, they make crowns for the heads of their gods.

text: Sometimes also the priests convey from their gods gold and silver, and bestow it upon themselves.
text_marked: Sometimes also the priests convey from their gods gold and silver, and bestow it upon themselves.

text: Yea, they will give thereof to the common harlots, and deck them as men with garments, being gods of silver, and gods of gold, and wood.
text_marked: Yea, they will give thereof to the common harlots, and deck them as men with garments, [being] gods of silver, and gods of gold, and wood.

text: Yet cannot these gods save themselves from rust and moth, though they be covered with purple raiment.
text_marked: Yet cannot these gods save themselves from rust and moth, though they be covered with purple raiment.

text: They wipe their faces because of the dust of the temple, when there is much upon them.
text_marked: They wipe their faces because of the dust of the temple, when there is much upon them.

text: And he that cannot put to death one that offendeth him holdeth a sceptre, as though he were a judge of the country.
text_marked: And he that cannot put to death one that offendeth him holdeth a sceptre, as though he were a judge of the country.

text: He hath also in his right hand a dagger and an ax: but cannot deliver himself from war and thieves.
text_marked: He hath also in his right hand a dagger and an ax: but cannot deliver himself from war and thieves.

text: Whereby they are known not to be gods: therefore fear them not.
text_marked: Whereby they are known not to be gods: therefore fear them not.

text: For like as a vessel that a man useth is nothing worth when it is broken; even so it is with their gods: when they be set up in the temple, their eyes be full of dust through the feet of them that come in.
text_marked: For like as a vessel that a man useth is nothing worth when it is broken; even so it is with their gods: when they be set up in the temple, their eyes be full of dust through the feet of them that come in.

text: And as the doors are made sure on every side upon him that offendeth the king, as being committed to suffer death: even so the priests make fast their temples with doors, with locks, and bars, lest their gods be spoiled with robbers.
text_marked: And as the doors are made sure on every side upon him that offendeth the king, as being committed to suffer death: even so the priests make fast their temples with doors, with locks, and bars, lest their gods be spoiled with robbers.

text: They light them candles, yea, more than for themselves, whereof they cannot see one.
text_marked: They light them candles, yea, more than for themselves, whereof they cannot see one.

text: They are as one of the beams of the temple, yet they say their hearts are gnawed upon by things creeping out of the earth; and when they eat them and their clothes, they feel it not.
text_marked: They are as one of the beams of the temple, yet they say their hearts are gnawed upon by things creeping out of the earth; and when they eat them and their clothes, they feel it not.

text: Their faces are blacked through the smoke that cometh out of the temple.
text_marked: Their faces are blacked through the smoke that cometh out of the temple.

text: Upon their bodies and heads sit bats, swallows, and birds, and the cats also.
text_marked: Upon their bodies and heads sit bats, swallows, and birds, and the cats also.

text: By this ye may know that they are no gods: therefore fear them not.
text_marked: By this ye may know that they are no gods: therefore fear them not.

text: Notwithstanding the gold that is about them to make them beautiful, except they wipe off the rust, they will not shine: for neither when they were molten did they feel it.
text_marked: Notwithstanding the gold that is about them to make them beautiful, except they wipe off the rust, they will not shine: for neither when they were molten did they feel it.

text: The things wherein there is no breath are bought for a most high price.
text_marked: The things wherein there is no breath are bought for a most high price.

text: They are borne upon shoulders, having no feet whereby they declare unto men that they be nothing worth.
text_marked: They are borne upon shoulders, having no feet whereby they declare unto men that they be nothing worth.

text: They also that serve them are ashamed: for if they fall to the ground at any time, they cannot rise up again of themselves: neither, if one set them upright, can they move of themselves: neither, if they be bowed down, can they make themselves straight: but they set gifts before them as unto dead men.
text_marked: They also that serve them are ashamed: for if they fall to the ground at any time, they cannot rise up again of themselves: neither, if one set them upright, can they move of themselves: neither, if they be bowed down, can they make themselves straight: but they set gifts before them as unto dead men.

text: As for the things that are sacrificed unto them, their priests sell and abuse; in like manner their wives lay up part thereof in salt; but unto the poor and impotent they give nothing of it.
text_marked: As for the things that are sacrificed unto them, their priests sell and abuse; in like manner their wives lay up part thereof in salt; but unto the poor and impotent they give nothing of it.

text: Menstruous women and women in childbed eat their sacrifices: by these things ye may know that they are no gods: fear them not.
text_marked: Menstruous women and women in childbed eat their sacrifices: by these things ye may know that they are no gods: fear them not.

text: For how can they be called gods? because women set meat before the gods of silver, gold, and wood.
text_marked: For how can they be called gods? because women set meat before the gods of silver, gold, and wood.

text: And the priests sit in their temples, having their clothes rent, and their heads and beards shaven, and nothing upon their heads.
text_marked: And the priests sit in their temples, having their clothes rent, and their heads and beards shaven, and nothing upon their heads.

text: They roar and cry before their gods, as men do at the feast when one is dead.
text_marked: They roar and cry before their gods, as men do at the feast when one is dead.

text: The priests also take off their garments, and clothe their wives and children.
text_marked: The priests also take off their garments, and clothe their wives and children.

text: Whether it be evil that one doeth unto them, or good, they are not able to recompense it: they can neither set up a king, nor put him down.
text_marked: Whether it be evil that one doeth unto them, or good, they are not able to recompense it: they can neither set up a king, nor put him down.

text: In like manner, they can neither give riches nor money: though a man make a vow unto them, and keep it not, they will not require it.
text_marked: In like manner, they can neither give riches nor money: though a man make a vow unto them, and keep it not, they will not require it.

text: They can save no man from death, neither deliver the weak from the mighty.
text_marked: They can save no man from death, neither deliver the weak from the mighty.

text: They cannot restore a blind man to his sight, nor help any man in his distress.
text_marked: They cannot restore a blind man to his sight, nor help any man in his distress.

text: They can shew no mercy to the widow, nor do good to the fatherless.
text_marked: They can shew no mercy to the widow, nor do good to the fatherless.

text: Their gods of wood, and which are overlaid with gold and silver, are like the stones that be hewn out of the mountain: they that worship them shall be confounded.
text_marked: Their gods of wood, and which are overlaid with gold and silver, are like the stones that be hewn out of the mountain: they that worship them shall be confounded.

text: How should a man then think and say that they are gods, when even the Chaldeans themselves dishonour them?
text_marked: How should a man then think and say that they are gods, when even the Chaldeans themselves dishonour them?

text: Who if they shall see one dumb that cannot speak, they bring him, and intreat Bel that he may speak, as though he were able to understand.
text_marked: Who if they shall see one dumb that cannot speak, they bring him, and intreat Bel that he may speak, as though he were able to understand.

text: Yet they cannot understand this themselves, and leave them: for they have no knowledge.
text_marked: Yet they cannot understand this themselves, and leave them: for they have no knowledge.

text: The women also with cords about them, sitting in the ways, burn bran for perfume: but if any of them, drawn by some that passeth by, lie with him, she reproacheth her fellow, that she was not thought as worthy as herself, nor her cord broken.
text_marked: The women also with cords about them, sitting in the ways, burn bran for perfume: but if any of them, drawn by some that passeth by, lie with him, she reproacheth her fellow, that she was not thought as worthy as herself, nor her cord broken.

text: Whatsoever is done among them is false: how may it then be thought or said that they are gods?
text_marked: Whatsoever is done among them is false: how may it then be thought or said that they are gods?

text: They are made of carpenters and goldsmiths: they can be nothing else than the workmen will have them to be.
text_marked: They are made of carpenters and goldsmiths: they can be nothing else than the workmen will have them to be.

text: And they themselves that made them can never continue long; how should then the things that are made of them be gods?
text_marked: And they themselves that made them can never continue long; how should then the things that are made of them be gods?

text: For they left lies and reproaches to them that come after.
text_marked: For they left lies and reproaches to them that come after.

text: For when there cometh any war or plague upon them, the priests consult with themselves, where they may be hidden with them.
text_marked: For when there cometh any war or plague upon them, the priests consult with themselves, where they may be hidden with them.

text: How then cannot men perceive that they be no gods, which can neither save themselves from war, nor from plague?
text_marked: How then cannot men perceive that they be no gods, which can neither save themselves from war, nor from plague?

text: For seeing they be but of wood, and overlaid with silver and gold, it shall be known hereafter that they are false:
text_marked: For seeing they be but of wood, and overlaid with silver and gold, it shall be known hereafter that they are false:

text: And it shall manifestly appear to all nations and kings that they are no gods, but the works of men’s hands, and that there is no work of God in them.
text_marked: And it shall manifestly appear to all nations and kings that they are no gods, but the works of men’s hands, and that there is no work of God in them.

text: Who then may not know that they are no gods?
text_marked: Who then may not know that they are no gods?

text: For neither can they set up a king in the land, nor give rain unto men.
text_marked: For neither can they set up a king in the land, nor give rain unto men.

text: Neither can they judge their own cause, nor redress a wrong, being unable: for they are as crows between heaven and earth.
text_marked: Neither can they judge their own cause, nor redress a wrong, being unable: for they are as crows between heaven and earth.

text: Whereupon when fire falleth upon the house of gods of wood, or laid over with gold or silver, their priests will flee away, and escape; but they themselves shall be burned asunder like beams.
text_marked: Whereupon when fire falleth upon the house of gods of wood, or laid over with gold or silver, their priests will flee away, and escape; but they themselves shall be burned asunder like beams.

text: Moreover they cannot withstand any king or enemies: how can it then be thought or said that they be gods?
text_marked: Moreover they cannot withstand any king or enemies: how can it then be thought or said that they be gods?

text: Neither are those gods of wood, and laid over with silver or gold, able to escape either from thieves or robbers.
text_marked: Neither are those gods of wood, and laid over with silver or gold, able to escape either from thieves or robbers.

text: Whose gold, and silver, and garments wherewith they are clothed, they that are strong take, and go away withal: neither are they able to help themselves.
text_marked: Whose gold, and silver, and garments wherewith they are clothed, they that are strong take, and go away withal: neither are they able to help themselves.

text: Therefore it is better to be a king that sheweth his power, or else a profitable vessel in an house, which the owner shall have use of, than such false gods; or to be a door in an house, to keep such things therein, than such false gods. or a pillar of wood in a palace, than such false gods.
text_marked: Therefore it is better to be a king that sheweth his power, or else a profitable vessel in an house, which the owner shall have use of, than such false gods; or to be a door in an house, to keep such things therein, than such false gods. or a pillar of wood in a palace, than such false gods.

text: For sun, moon, and stars, being bright and sent to do their offices, are obedient.
text_marked: For sun, moon, and stars, being bright and sent to do their offices, are obedient.

text: In like manner the lightning when it breaketh forth is easy to be seen; and after the same manner the wind bloweth in every country.
text_marked: In like manner the lightning when it breaketh forth is easy to be seen; and after the same manner the wind bloweth in every country.

text: And when God commandeth the clouds to go over the whole world, they do as they are bidden.
text_marked: And when God commandeth the clouds to go over the whole world, they do as they are bidden.

text: And the fire sent from above to consume hills and woods doeth as it is commanded: but these are like unto them neither in shew nor power.
text_marked: And the fire sent from above to consume hills and woods doeth as it is commanded: but these are like unto them neither in shew nor power.

text: Wherefore it is neither to be supposed nor said that they are gods, seeing, they are able neither to judge causes, nor to do good unto men.
text_marked: Wherefore it is neither to be supposed nor said that they are gods, seeing, they are able neither to judge causes, nor to do good unto men.

text: Knowing therefore that they are no gods, fear them not,
text_marked: Knowing therefore that they are no gods, fear them not,

text: For they can neither curse nor bless kings:
text_marked: For they can neither curse nor bless kings:

text: Neither can they shew signs in the heavens among the heathen, nor shine as the sun, nor give light as the moon.
text_marked: Neither can they shew signs in the heavens among the heathen, nor shine as the sun, nor give light as the moon.

text: The beasts are better than they: for they can get under a cover and help themselves.
text_marked: The beasts are better than they: for they can get under a cover and help themselves.

text: It is then by no means manifest unto us that they are gods: therefore fear them not.
text_marked: It is then by no means manifest unto us that they are gods: therefore fear them not.

text: For as a scarecrow in a garden of cucumbers keepeth nothing: so are their gods of wood, and laid over with silver and gold.
text_marked: For as a scarecrow in a garden of cucumbers keepeth nothing: so are their gods of wood, and laid over with silver and gold.

text: And likewise their gods of wood, and laid over with silver and gold, are like to a white thorn in an orchard, that every bird sitteth upon; as also to a dead body, that is cast into the dark.
text_marked: And likewise their gods of wood, and laid over with silver and gold, are like to a white thorn in an orchard, that every bird sitteth upon; as also to a dead body, that is cast into the dark.

text: And ye shall know them to be no gods by the bright purple that rotteth upon them: and they themselves afterward shall be eaten, and shall be a reproach in the country.
text_marked: And ye shall know them to be no gods by the bright purple that rotteth upon them: and they themselves afterward shall be eaten, and shall be a reproach in the country.

text: Better therefore is the just man that hath none idols: for he shall be far from reproach.
text_marked: Better therefore is the just man that hath none idols: for he shall be far from reproach.

ref: Prayer of Azariah and Song of the Three 1:3
text: Blessed art thou, O Lord God of our fathers: thy name is worthy to be praised and glorified for evermore:
text_marked: Blessed art thou, O Lord God of our fathers: thy name is worthy to be praised and glorified for evermore:

book_name: Prayer of Azariah and Song of the Three
ref: Prayer of Azariah and Song of the Three 1:4
text: For thou art righteous in all the things that thou hast done to us: yea, true are all thy works, thy ways are right, and all thy judgments truth.
text_marked: For thou art righteous in all the things that thou hast done to us: yea, true are all thy works, thy ways are right, and all thy judgments truth.

book_name: Prayer of Azariah and Song of the Three
ref: Prayer of Azariah and Song of the Three 1:5
text: In all the things that thou hast brought upon us, and upon the holy city of our fathers, even Jerusalem, thou hast executed true judgment: for according to truth and judgment didst thou bring all these things upon us because of our sins.
text_marked: In all the things that thou hast brought upon us, and upon the holy city of our fathers, even Jerusalem, thou hast executed true judgment: for according to truth and judgment didst thou bring all these things upon us because of our sins.

book_name: Prayer of Azariah and Song of the Three
ref: Prayer of Azariah and Song of the Three 1:6
text: For we have sinned and committed iniquity, departing from thee.
text_marked: For we have sinned and committed iniquity, departing from thee.

book_name: Prayer of Azariah and Song of the Three
ref: Prayer of Azariah and Song of the Three 1:7
text: In all things have we trespassed, and not obeyed thy commandments, nor kept them, neither done as thou hast commanded us, that it might go well with us.
text_marked: In all things have we trespassed, and not obeyed thy commandments, nor kept them, neither done as thou hast commanded us, that it might go well with us.

book_name: Prayer of Azariah and Song of the Three
ref: Prayer of Azariah and Song of the Three 1:8
text: Wherefore all that thou hast brought upon us, and every thing that thou hast done to us, thou hast done in true judgment.
text_marked: Wherefore all that thou hast brought upon us, and every thing that thou hast done to us, thou hast done in true judgment.

book_name: Prayer of Azariah and Song of the Three
ref: Prayer of Azariah and Song of the Three 1:9
text: And thou didst deliver us into the hands of lawless enemies, most hateful forsakers of God, and to an unjust king, and the most wicked in all the world.
text_marked: And thou didst deliver us into the hands of lawless enemies, most hateful forsakers of God, and to an unjust king, and the most wicked in all the world.

book_name: Prayer of Azariah and Song of the Three
ref: Prayer of Azariah and Song of the Three 1:10

text_marked: And now we cannot open our mouths, we are become a shame and reproach to thy servants; and to them that worship thee.

text_marked: Yet deliver us not up wholly, for thy name’s sake, neither disannul thou thy covenant:

book_name: Prayer of Azariah and Song of the Three
ref: Prayer of Azariah and Song of the Three 1:12

text_marked: And cause not thy mercy to depart from us, for thy beloved Abraham’s sake, for thy servant Issac’s sake, and for thy holy Israel’s sake;

text_marked: For we, O Lord, are become less than any nation, and be kept under this day in all the world because of our sins.

text: There dwelt a man in Babylon, called Joacim:
text_marked: There dwelt a man in Babylon, called Joacim:

text: And he took a wife, whose name was Susanna, the daughter of Chelcias, a very fair woman, and one that feared the Lord.
text_marked: And he took a wife, whose name was Susanna, the daughter of Chelcias, a very fair woman, and one that feared the Lord.

text: Her parents also were righteous, and taught their daughter according to the law of Moses.
text_marked: Her parents also were righteous, and taught their daughter according to the law of Moses.

text: Now Joacim was a great rich man, and had a fair garden joining unto his house: and to him resorted the Jews; because he was more honourable than all others.
text_marked: Now Joacim was a great rich man, and had a fair garden joining unto his house: and to him resorted the Jews; because he was more honourable than all others.

text: The same year were appointed two of the ancients of the people to be judges, such as the Lord spake of, that wickedness came from Babylon from ancient judges, who seemed to govern the people.
text_marked: The same year were appointed two of the ancients of the people to be judges, such as the Lord spake of, that wickedness came from Babylon from ancient judges, who seemed to govern the people.

text: These kept much at Joacim’s house: and all that had any suits in law came unto them.
text_marked: These kept much at Joacim’s house: and all that had any suits in law came unto them.

text: Now when the people departed away at noon, Susanna went into her husband’s garden to walk.
text_marked: Now when the people departed away at noon, Susanna went into her husband’s garden to walk.

text: And the two elders saw her going in every day, and walking; so that their lust was inflamed toward her.
text_marked: And the two elders saw her going in every day, and walking; so that their lust was inflamed toward her.

text: And they perverted their own mind, and turned away their eyes, that they might not look unto heaven, nor remember just judgments.
text_marked: And they perverted their own mind, and turned away their eyes, that they might not look unto heaven, nor remember just judgments.

text: And albeit they both were wounded with her love, yet durst not one shew another his grief.
text_marked: And albeit they both were wounded with her love, yet durst not one shew another his grief.

text: For they were ashamed to declare their lust, that they desired to have to do with her.
text_marked: For they were ashamed to declare their lust, that they desired to have to do with her.

text: Yet they watched diligently from day to day to see her.
text_marked: Yet they watched diligently from day to day to see her.

text: And the one said to the other, Let us now go home: for it is dinner time.
text_marked: And the one said to the other, Let us now go home: for it is dinner time.

text: So when they were gone out, they parted the one from the other, and turning back again they came to the same place; and after that they had asked one another the cause, they acknowledged their lust: then appointed they a time both together, when they might find her alone.
text_marked: So when they were gone out, they parted the one from the other, and turning back again they came to the same place; and after that they had asked one another the cause, they acknowledged their lust: then appointed they a time both together, when they might find her alone.

text: And it fell out, as they watched a fit time, she went in as before with two maids only, and she was desirous to wash herself in the garden: for it was hot.
text_marked: And it fell out, as they watched a fit time, she went in as before with two maids only, and she was desirous to wash herself in the garden: for it was hot.

text: And there was no body there save the two elders, that had hid themselves, and watched her.
text_marked: And there was no body there save the two elders, that had hid themselves, and watched her.

text: Then she said to her maids, Bring me oil and washing balls, and shut the garden doors, that I may wash me.
text_marked: Then she said to her maids, Bring me oil and washing balls, and shut the garden doors, that I may wash me.

text: And they did as she bade them, and shut the garden doors, and went out themselves at privy doors to fetch the things that she had commanded them: but they saw not the elders, because they were hid.
text_marked: And they did as she bade them, and shut the garden doors, and went out themselves at privy doors to fetch the things that she had commanded them: but they saw not the elders, because they were hid.

text: Now when the maids were gone forth, the two elders rose up, and ran unto her, saying,
text_marked: Now when the maids were gone forth, the two elders rose up, and ran unto her, saying,

text: Behold, the garden doors are shut, that no man can see us, and we are in love with thee; therefore consent unto us, and lie with us.
text_marked: Behold, the garden doors are shut, that no man can see us, and we are in love with thee; therefore consent unto us, and lie with us.

text: If thou wilt not, we will bear witness against thee, that a young man was with thee: and therefore thou didst send away thy maids from thee.
text_marked: If thou wilt not, we will bear witness against thee, that a young man was with thee: and therefore thou didst send away thy maids from thee.

text: Then Susanna sighed, and said, I am straitened on every side: for if I do this thing, it is death unto me: and if I do it not I cannot escape your hands.
text_marked: Then Susanna sighed, and said, I am straitened on every side: for if I do this thing, it is death unto me: and if I do it not I cannot escape your hands.

text: It is better for me to fall into your hands, and not do it, than to sin in the sight of the Lord.
text_marked: It is better for me to fall into your hands, and not do it, than to sin in the sight of the Lord.

text: With that Susanna cried with a loud voice: and the two elders cried out against her.
text_marked: With that Susanna cried with a loud voice: and the two elders cried out against her.

text: Then ran the one, and opened the garden door.
text_marked: Then ran the one, and opened the garden door.

text: So when the servants of the house heard the cry in the garden, they rushed in at the privy door, to see what was done unto her.
text_marked: So when the servants of the house heard the cry in the garden, they rushed in at the privy door, to see what was done unto her.

text: But when the elders had declared their matter, the servants were greatly ashamed: for there was never such a report made of Susanna.
text_marked: But when the elders had declared their matter, the servants were greatly ashamed: for there was never such a report made of Susanna.

text: And it came to pass the next day, when the people were assembled to her husband Joacim, the two elders came also full of mischievous imagination against Susanna to put her to death;
text_marked: And it came to pass the next day, when the people were assembled to her husband Joacim, the two elders came also full of mischievous imagination against Susanna to put her to death;

text: And said before the people, Send for Susanna, the daughter of Chelcias, Joacim’s wife. And so they sent.
text_marked: And said before the people, Send for Susanna, the daughter of Chelcias, Joacim’s wife. And so they sent.

text: So she came with her father and mother, her children, and all her kindred.
text_marked: So she came with her father and mother, her children, and all her kindred.

text: Now Susanna was a very delicate woman, and beauteous to behold.
text_marked: Now Susanna was a very delicate woman, and beauteous to behold.

text: And these wicked men commanded to uncover her face, (for she was covered) that they might be filled with her beauty.
text_marked: And these wicked men commanded to uncover her face, (for she was covered) that they might be filled with her beauty.

text: Therefore her friends and all that saw her wept.
text_marked: Therefore her friends and all that saw her wept.

text: Then the two elders stood up in the midst of the people, and laid their hands upon her head.
text_marked: Then the two elders stood up in the midst of the people, and laid their hands upon her head.

text: And she weeping looked up toward heaven: for her heart trusted in the Lord.
text_marked: And she weeping looked up toward heaven: for her heart trusted in the Lord.

text: And the elders said, As we walked in the garden alone, this woman came in with two maids, and shut the garden doors, and sent the maids away.
text_marked: And the elders said, As we walked in the garden alone, this woman came in with two maids, and shut the garden doors, and sent the maids away.

text: Then a young man, who there was hid, came unto her, and lay with her.
text_marked: Then a young man, who there was hid, came unto her, and lay with her.

text: Then we that stood in a corner of the garden, seeing this wickedness, ran unto them.
text_marked: Then we that stood in a corner of the garden, seeing this wickedness, ran unto them.

text: And when we saw them together, the man we could not hold: for he was stronger than we, and opened the door, and leaped out.
text_marked: And when we saw them together, the man we could not hold: for he was stronger than we, and opened the door, and leaped out.

text: But having taken this woman, we asked who the young man was, but she would not tell us: these things do we testify.
text_marked: But having taken this woman, we asked who the young man was, but she would not tell us: these things do we testify.

text: Then the assembly believed them as those that were the elders and judges of the people: so they condemned her to death.
text_marked: Then the assembly believed them as those that were the elders and judges of the people: so they condemned her to death.

text: Then Susanna cried out with a loud voice, and said, O everlasting God, that knowest the secrets, and knowest all things before they be:
text_marked: Then Susanna cried out with a loud voice, and said, O everlasting God, that knowest the secrets, and knowest all things before they be:

text: Thou knowest that they have borne false witness against me, and, behold, I must die; whereas I never did such things as these men have maliciously invented against me.
text_marked: Thou knowest that they have borne false witness against me, and, behold, I must die; whereas I never did such things as these men have maliciously invented against me.

text: And the Lord heard her voice.
text_marked: And the Lord heard her voice.

text: Therefore when she was led to be put to death, the Lord raised up the holy spirit of a young youth whose name was Daniel:
text_marked: Therefore when she was led to be put to death, the Lord raised up the holy spirit of a young youth whose name was Daniel:

text: Who cried with a loud voice, I am clear from the blood of this woman.
text_marked: Who cried with a loud voice, I am clear from the blood of this woman.

text: Then all the people turned them toward him, and said, What mean these words that thou hast spoken?
text_marked: Then all the people turned them toward him, and said, What mean these words that thou hast spoken?

text: So he standing in the midst of them said, Are ye such fools, ye sons of Israel, that without examination or knowledge of the truth ye have condemned a daughter of Israel?
text_marked: So he standing in the midst of them said, Are ye such fools, ye sons of Israel, that without examination or knowledge of the truth ye have condemned a daughter of Israel?

text: Return again to the place of judgment: for they have borne false witness against her.
text_marked: Return again to the place of judgment: for they have borne false witness against her.

text: Wherefore all the people turned again in haste, and the elders said unto him, Come, sit down among us, and shew it us, seeing God hath given thee the honour of an elder.
text_marked: Wherefore all the people turned again in haste, and the elders said unto him, Come, sit down among us, and shew it us, seeing God hath given thee the honour of an elder.

text: Then said Daniel unto them, Put these two aside one far from another, and I will examine them.
text_marked: Then said Daniel unto them, Put these two aside one far from another, and I will examine them.

text: So when they were put asunder one from another, he called one of them, and said unto him, O thou that art waxen old in wickedness, now thy sins which thou hast committed aforetime are come to light.
text_marked: So when they were put asunder one from another, he called one of them, and said unto him, O thou that art waxen old in wickedness, now thy sins which thou hast committed aforetime are come to light.

text: For thou hast pronounced false judgment and hast condemned the innocent and hast let the guilty go free; albeit the Lord saith, The innocent and righteous shalt thou not slay.
text_marked: For thou hast pronounced false judgment and hast condemned the innocent and hast let the guilty go free; albeit the Lord saith, The innocent and righteous shalt thou not slay.

text: Now then, if thou hast seen her, tell me, Under what tree sawest thou them companying together? Who answered, Under a mastick tree.
text_marked: Now then, if thou hast seen her, tell me, Under what tree sawest thou them companying together? Who answered, Under a mastick tree.

text: And Daniel said, Very well; thou hast lied against thine own head; for even now the angel of God hath received the sentence of God to cut thee in two.
text_marked: And Daniel said, Very well; thou hast lied against thine own head; for even now the angel of God hath received the sentence of God to cut thee in two.

text: So he put him aside, and commanded to bring the other, and said unto him, O thou seed of Chanaan, and not of Juda, beauty hath deceived thee, and lust hath perverted thine heart.
text_marked: So he put him aside, and commanded to bring the other, and said unto him, O thou seed of Chanaan, and not of Juda, beauty hath deceived thee, and lust hath perverted thine heart.

text: Thus have ye dealt with the daughters of Israel, and they for fear companied with you: but the daughter of Juda would not abide your wickedness.
text_marked: Thus have ye dealt with the daughters of Israel, and they for fear companied with you: but the daughter of Juda would not abide your wickedness.

text: Now therefore tell me, Under what tree didst thou take them companying together? Who answered, Under an holm tree.
text_marked: Now therefore tell me, Under what tree didst thou take them companying together? Who answered, Under an holm tree.

text: Then said Daniel unto him, Well; thou hast also lied against thine own head: for the angel of God waiteth with the sword to cut thee in two, that he may destroy you.
text_marked: Then said Daniel unto him, Well; thou hast also lied against thine own head: for the angel of God waiteth with the sword to cut thee in two, that he may destroy you.

text: With that all the assembly cried out with a loud voice, and praised God, who saveth them that trust in him.
text_marked: With that all the assembly cried out with a loud voice, and praised God, who saveth them that trust in him.

text: And they arose against the two elders, for Daniel had convicted them of false witness by their own mouth:
text_marked: And they arose against the two elders, for Daniel had convicted them of false witness by their own mouth:

text: And according to the law of Moses they did unto them in such sort as they maliciously intended to do to their neighbour: and they put them to death. Thus the innocent blood was saved the same day.
text_marked: And according to the law of Moses they did unto them in such sort as they maliciously intended to do to their neighbour: and they put them to death. Thus the innocent blood was saved the same day.

text: Therefore Chelcias and his wife praised God for their daughter Susanna, with Joacim her husband, and all the kindred, because there was no dishonesty found in her.
text_marked: Therefore Chelcias and his wife praised God for their daughter Susanna, with Joacim her husband, and all the kindred, because there was no dishonesty found in her.

text: From that day forth was Daniel had in great reputation in the sight of the people.
text_marked: From that day forth was Daniel had in great reputation in the sight of the people.

text: And king Astyages was gathered to his fathers, and Cyrus of Persia received his kingdom.
text_marked: And king Astyages was gathered to his fathers, and Cyrus of Persia received his kingdom.

text: And Daniel conversed with the king, and was honoured above all his friends.
text_marked: And Daniel conversed with the king, and was honoured above all his friends.

text: Now the Babylons had an idol, called Bel, and there were spent upon him every day twelve great measures of fine flour, and forty sheep, and six vessels of wine.
text_marked: Now the Babylons had an idol, called Bel, and there were spent upon him every day twelve great measures of fine flour, and forty sheep, and six vessels of wine.

text: And the king worshipped it and went daily to adore it: but Daniel worshipped his own God. And the king said unto him, Why dost not thou worship Bel?
text_marked: And the king worshipped it and went daily to adore it: but Daniel worshipped his own God. And the king said unto him, Why dost not thou worship Bel?

text: Who answered and said, Because I may not worship idols made with hands, but the living God, who hath created the heaven and the earth, and hath sovereignty over all flesh.
text_marked: Who answered and said, Because I may not worship idols made with hands, but the living God, who hath created the heaven and the earth, and hath sovereignty over all flesh.

text: Then said the king unto him, Thinkest thou not that Bel is a living God? seest thou not how much he eateth and drinketh every day?
text_marked: Then said the king unto him, Thinkest thou not that Bel is a living God? seest thou not how much he eateth and drinketh every day?

text: Then Daniel smiled, and said, O king, be not deceived: for this is but clay within, and brass without, and did never eat or drink any thing.
text_marked: Then Daniel smiled, and said, O king, be not deceived: for this is but clay within, and brass without, and did never eat or drink any thing.

text: So the king was wroth, and called for his priests, and said unto them, If ye tell me not who this is that devoureth these expences, ye shall die.
text_marked: So the king was wroth, and called for his priests, and said unto them, If ye tell me not who this is that devoureth these expences, ye shall die.

text: But if ye can certify me that Bel devoureth them, then Daniel shall die: for he hath spoken blasphemy against Bel. And Daniel said unto the king, Let it be according to thy word.
text_marked: But if ye can certify me that Bel devoureth them, then Daniel shall die: for he hath spoken blasphemy against Bel. And Daniel said unto the king, Let it be according to thy word.

text: Now the priests of Bel were threescore and ten, beside their wives and children. And the king went with Daniel into the temple of Bel.
text_marked: Now the priests of Bel were threescore and ten, beside their wives and children. And the king went with Daniel into the temple of Bel.

text: So Bel’s priests said, Lo, we go out: but thou, O king, set on the meat, and make ready the wine, and shut the door fast and seal it with thine own signet;
text_marked: So Bel’s priests said, Lo, we go out: but thou, O king, set on the meat, and make ready the wine, and shut the door fast and seal it with thine own signet;

text: And to morrow when thou comest in, if thou findest not that Bel hath eaten up all, we will suffer death: or else Daniel, that speaketh falsely against us.
text_marked: And to morrow when thou comest in, if thou findest not that Bel hath eaten up all, we will suffer death: or else Daniel, that speaketh falsely against us.

text: And they little regarded it: for under the table they had made a privy entrance, whereby they entered in continually, and consumed those things.
text_marked: And they little regarded it: for under the table they had made a privy entrance, whereby they entered in continually, and consumed those things.

text: So when they were gone forth, the king set meats before Bel. Now Daniel had commanded his servants to bring ashes, and those they strewed throughout all the temple in the presence of the king alone: then went they out, and shut the door, and sealed it with the king’s signet, and so departed.
text_marked: So when they were gone forth, the king set meats before Bel. text: Now in the night came the priests with their wives and children, as they were wont to do, and did eat and drink up all.
text_marked: Now in the night came the priests with their wives and children, as they were wont to do, and did eat and drink up all.

text: In the morning betime the king arose, and Daniel with him.

text: And the king said, Daniel, are the seals whole? And he said, Yea, O king, they be whole.
text_marked: And the king said, Daniel, are the seals whole? And he said, Yea, O king, they be whole.

text: And as soon as he had opened the door, the king looked upon the table, and cried with a loud voice, Great art thou, O Bel, and with thee is no deceit at all.
text_marked: And as soon as he had opened the door, the king looked upon the table, and cried with a loud voice, Great art thou, O Bel, and with thee is no deceit at all.

text: Then laughed Daniel, and held the king that he should not go in, and said, Behold now the pavement, and mark well whose footsteps are these.
text_marked: Then laughed Daniel, and held the king that he should not go in, and said, Behold now the pavement, and mark well whose footsteps are these.

text_marked: And took the priests with their wives and children, who shewed him the privy doors, where they came in, and consumed such things as were upon the table.

text: Therefore the king slew them, and delivered Bel into Daniel’s power, who destroyed him and his temple.
text_marked: Therefore the king slew them, and delivered Bel into Daniel’s power, who destroyed him and his temple.

text: And in that same place there was a great dragon, which they of Babylon worshipped.
text_marked: And in that same place there was a great dragon, which they of Babylon worshipped.

text: And the king said unto Daniel, Wilt thou also say that this is of brass? lo, he liveth, he eateth and drinketh; thou canst not say that he is no living god: therefore worship him.
text_marked: And the king said unto Daniel, Wilt thou also say that this is of brass? lo, he liveth, he eateth and drinketh; thou canst not say that he is no living god: therefore worship him.

text: Then said Daniel unto the king, I will worship the Lord my God: for he is the living God.
text_marked: Then said Daniel unto the king, I will worship the Lord my God: for he is the living God.

text: But give me leave, O king, and I shall slay this dragon without sword or staff. The king said, I give thee leave.
text_marked: But give me leave, O king, and I shall slay this dragon without sword or staff. The king said, I give thee leave.

text: Then Daniel took pitch, and fat, and hair, and did seethe them together, and made lumps thereof: this he put in the dragon’s mouth, and so the dragon burst in sunder: and Daniel said, Lo, these are the gods ye worship.
text_marked: Then Daniel took pitch, and fat, and hair, and did seethe them together, and made lumps thereof: this he put in the dragon’s mouth, and so the dragon burst in sunder: and Daniel said, Lo, these are the gods ye worship.

text: When they of Babylon heard that, they took great indignation, and conspired against the king, saying, The king is become a Jew, and he hath destroyed Bel, he hath slain the dragon, and put the priests to death.
text_marked: When they of Babylon heard that, they took great indignation, and conspired against the king, saying, The king is become a Jew, and he hath destroyed Bel, he hath slain the dragon, and put the priests to death.

text: So they came to the king, and said, Deliver us Daniel, or else we will destroy thee and thine house.

text: Now when the king saw that they pressed him sore, being constrained, he delivered Daniel unto them:
