text: Thus he that had driven many out of their country perished in a strange land, retiring to the Lacedemonians, and thinking there to find succour by reason of his kindred:
text_marked: Thus he that had driven many out of their country perished in a strange land, retiring to the Lacedemonians, and thinking there to find succour by reason of his kindred:

text: And he that had cast out many unburied had none to mourn for him, nor any solemn funerals at all, nor sepulchre with his fathers.
text_marked: And he that had cast out many unburied had none to mourn for him, nor any solemn funerals at all, nor sepulchre with his fathers.

text: Now when this that was done came to the king’s ear, he thought that Judea had revolted: whereupon removing out of Egypt in a furious mind, he took the city by force of arms,
text_marked: Now when this that was done came to the king’s ear, he thought that Judea had revolted: whereupon removing out of Egypt in a furious mind, he took the city by force of arms,

text: And commanded his men of war not to spare such as they met, and to slay such as went up upon the houses.
text_marked: And commanded his men of war not to spare such as they met, and to slay such as went up upon the houses.

text: Thus there was killing of young and old, making away of men, women, and children, slaying of virgins and infants.
text_marked: Thus there was killing of young and old, making away of men, women, and children, slaying of virgins and infants.

text: And there were destroyed within the space of three whole days fourscore thousand, whereof forty thousand were slain in the conflict; and no fewer sold than slain.
text_marked: And there were destroyed within the space of three whole days fourscore thousand, whereof forty thousand were slain in the conflict; and no fewer sold than slain.

text: Yet was he not content with this, but presumed to go into the most holy temple of all the world; Menelaus, that traitor to the laws, and to his own country, being his guide:
text_marked: Yet was he not content with this, but presumed to go into the most holy temple of all the world; Menelaus, that traitor to the laws, and to his own country, being his guide:

text: And taking the holy vessels with polluted hands, and with profane hands pulling down the things that were dedicated by other kings to the augmentation and glory and honour of the place, he gave them away.
text_marked: And taking the holy vessels with polluted hands, and with profane hands pulling down the things that were dedicated by other kings to the augmentation and glory and honour of the place, he gave them away.

text: And so haughty was Antiochus in mind, that he considered not that the Lord was angry for a while for the sins of them that dwelt in the city, and therefore his eye was not upon the place.
text_marked: And so haughty was Antiochus in mind, that he considered not that the Lord was angry for a while for the sins of them that dwelt in the city, and therefore his eye was not upon the place.

text: For had they not been formerly wrapped in many sins, this man, as soon as he had come, had forthwith been scourged, and put back from his presumption, as Heliodorus was, whom Seleucus the king sent to view the treasury.
text_marked: For had they not been formerly wrapped in many sins, this man, as soon as he had come, had forthwith been scourged, and put back from his presumption, as Heliodorus was, whom Seleucus the king sent to view the treasury.

text: Nevertheless God did not choose the people for the place’s sake, but the place for the people’s sake.
text_marked: Nevertheless God did not choose the people for the place’s sake, but the place for the people’s sake.

text: And therefore the place itself, that was partaker with them of the adversity that happened to the nation, did afterward communicate in the benefits sent from the Lord: and as it was forsaken in the wrath of the Almighty, so again, the great Lord being reconciled, it was set up with all glory.
text_marked: And therefore the place itself, that was partaker with them of the adversity that happened to the nation, did afterward communicate in the benefits sent from the Lord: and as it was forsaken in the wrath of the Almighty, so again, the great Lord being reconciled, it was set up with all glory.

text: So when Antiochus had carried out of the temple a thousand and eight hundred talents, he departed in all haste unto Antiochia, weening in his pride to make the land navigable, and the sea passable by foot: such was the haughtiness of his mind.

text: And he left governors to vex the nation: at Jerusalem, Philip, for his country a Phrygian, and for manners more barbarous than he that set him there;
text_marked: And he left governors to vex the nation: at Jerusalem, Philip, for his country a Phrygian, and for manners more barbarous than he that set him there;

text: And at Garizim, Andronicus; and besides, Menelaus, who worse than all the rest bare an heavy hand over the citizens, having a malicious mind against his countrymen the Jews.
text_marked: And at Garizim, Andronicus; and besides, Menelaus, who worse than all the rest bare an heavy hand over the citizens, having a malicious mind against his countrymen the Jews.

text: He sent also that detestable ringleader Apollonius with an army of two and twenty thousand, commanding him to slay all those that were in their best age, and to sell the women and the younger sort:
text_marked: He sent also that detestable ringleader Apollonius with an army of two and twenty thousand, commanding him to slay all those that were in their best age, and to sell the women and the younger sort:

text: Who coming to Jerusalem, and pretending peace, did forbear till the holy day of the sabbath, when taking the Jews keeping holy day, he commanded his men to arm themselves.
text_marked: Who coming to Jerusalem, and pretending peace, did forbear till the holy day of the sabbath, when taking the Jews keeping holy day, he commanded his men to arm themselves.

text: And so he slew all them that were gone to the celebrating of the sabbath, and running through the city with weapons slew great multitudes.
text_marked: And so he slew all them that were gone to the celebrating of the sabbath, and running through the city with weapons slew great multitudes.

text: But Judas Maccabeus with nine others, or thereabout, withdrew himself into the wilderness, and lived in the mountains after the manner of beasts, with his company, who fed on herbs continually, lest they should be partakers of the pollution.
text_marked: But Judas Maccabeus with nine others, or thereabout, withdrew himself into the wilderness, and lived in the mountains after the manner of beasts, with his company, who fed on herbs continually, lest they should be partakers of the pollution.

text: Not long after this the king sent an old man of Athens to compel the Jews to depart from the laws of their fathers, and not to live after the laws of God:
text_marked: Not long after this the king sent an old man of Athens to compel the Jews to depart from the laws of their fathers, and not to live after the laws of God:

text: And to pollute also the temple in Jerusalem, and to call it the temple of Jupiter Olympius; and that in Garizim, of Jupiter the Defender of strangers, as they did desire that dwelt in the place.
text_marked: And to pollute also the temple in Jerusalem, and to call it the temple of Jupiter Olympius; and that in Garizim, of Jupiter the Defender of strangers, as they did desire that dwelt in the place.

text: The coming in of this mischief was sore and grievous to the people:
text_marked: The coming in of this mischief was sore and grievous to the people:

text: For the temple was filled with riot and revelling by the Gentiles, who dallied with harlots, and had to do with women within the circuit of the holy places, and besides that brought in things that were not lawful.
text_marked: For the temple was filled with riot and revelling by the Gentiles, who dallied with harlots, and had to do with women within the circuit of the holy places, and besides that brought in things that were not lawful.

text: The altar also was filled with profane things, which the law forbiddeth.
text_marked: The altar also was filled with profane things, which the law forbiddeth.

text: Neither was it lawful for a man to keep sabbath days or ancient fasts, or to profess himself at all to be a Jew.
text_marked: Neither was it lawful for a man to keep sabbath days or ancient fasts, or to profess himself at all to be a Jew.

text: And in the day of the king’s birth every month they were brought by bitter constraint to eat of the sacrifices; and when the fast of Bacchus was kept, the Jews were compelled to go in procession to Bacchus, carrying ivy.
text_marked: And in the day of the king’s birth every month they were brought by bitter constraint to eat of the sacrifices; and when the fast of Bacchus was kept, the Jews were compelled to go in procession to Bacchus, carrying ivy.

text: Moreover there went out a decree to the neighbour cities of the heathen, by the suggestion of Ptolemee, against the Jews, that they should observe the same fashions, and be partakers of their sacrifices:
text_marked: Moreover there went out a decree to the neighbour cities of the heathen, by the suggestion of Ptolemee, against the Jews, that they should observe the same fashions, and be partakers of their sacrifices:

text: And whoso would not conform themselves to the manners of the Gentiles should be put to death. Then might a man have seen the present misery.
text_marked: And whoso would not conform themselves to the manners of the Gentiles should be put to death. Then might a man have seen the present misery.

text: For there were two women brought, who had circumcised their children; whom when they had openly led round about the city, the babes hanging at their breasts, they cast them down headlong from the wall.
text_marked: For there were two women brought, who had circumcised their children; whom when they had openly led round about the city, the babes hanging at their breasts, they cast them down headlong from the wall.

text: And others, that had run together into caves near by, to keep the sabbath day secretly, being discovered by Philip, were all burnt together, because they made a conscience to help themselves for the honour of the most sacred day.
text_marked: And others, that had run together into caves near by, to keep the sabbath day secretly, being discovered by Philip, were all burnt together, because they made a conscience to help themselves for the honour of the most sacred day.

text: Now I beseech those that read this book, that they be not discouraged for these calamities, but that they judge those punishments not to be for destruction, but for a chastening of our nation.
text_marked: Now I beseech those that read this book, that they be not discouraged for these calamities, but that they judge those punishments not to be for destruction, but for a chastening of our nation.

text: For it is a token of his great goodness, when wicked doers are not suffered any long time, but forthwith punished.
text_marked: For it is a token of his great goodness, when wicked doers are not suffered any long time, but forthwith punished.

text: For not as with other nations, whom the Lord patiently forbeareth to punish, till they be come to the fulness of their sins, so dealeth he with us,
text_marked: For not as with other nations, whom the Lord patiently forbeareth to punish, till they be come to the fulness of their sins, so dealeth he with us,

text: Lest that, being come to the height of sin, afterwards he should take vengeance of us.
text_marked: Lest that, being come to the height of sin, afterwards he should take vengeance of us.

text: And therefore he never withdraweth his mercy from us: and though he punish with adversity, yet doth he never forsake his people.
text_marked: And therefore he never withdraweth his mercy from us: and though he punish with adversity, yet doth he never forsake his people.

text: But let this that we have spoken be for a warning unto us. And now will we come to the declaring of the matter in a few words.
text_marked: But let this that we have spoken be for a warning unto us. And now will we come to the declaring of the matter in a few words.

text: Eleazar, one of the principal scribes, an aged man, and of a well favoured countenance, was constrained to open his mouth, and to eat swine’s flesh.
text_marked: Eleazar, one of the principal scribes, an aged man, and of a well favoured countenance, was constrained to open his mouth, and to eat swine’s flesh.

text: But he, choosing rather to die gloriously, than to live stained with such an abomination, spit it forth, and came of his own accord to the torment,
text_marked: But he, choosing rather to die gloriously, than to live stained with such an abomination, spit it forth, and came of his own accord to the torment,

text: As it behoved them to come, that are resolute to stand out against such things, as are not lawful for love of life to be tasted.
text_marked: As it behoved them to come, that are resolute to stand out against such things, as are not lawful for love of life to be tasted.

text: But they that had the charge of that wicked feast, for the old acquaintance they had with the man, taking him aside, besought him to bring flesh of his own provision, such as was lawful for him to use, and make as if he did eat of the flesh taken from the sacrifice commanded by the king;
text_marked: But they that had the charge of that wicked feast, for the old acquaintance they had with the man, taking him aside, besought him to bring flesh of his own provision, such as was lawful for him to use, and make as if he did eat of the flesh taken from the sacrifice commanded by the king;

text: That in so doing he might be delivered from death, and for the old friendship with them find favour.
text_marked: That in so doing he might be delivered from death, and for the old friendship with them find favour.

text: But he began to consider discreetly, and as became his age, and the excellency of his ancient years, and the honour of his gray head, whereon was come, and his most honest education from a child, or rather the holy law made and given by God: therefore he answered accordingly, and willed them straightways to send him to the grave.
text_marked: But he began to consider discreetly, and as became his age, and the excellency of his ancient years, and the honour of his gray head, whereon was come, and his most honest education from a child, or rather the holy law made and given by God: therefore he answered accordingly, and willed them straightways to send him to the grave.

text: For it becometh not our age, said he, in any wise to dissemble, whereby many young persons might think that Eleazar, being fourscore years old and ten, were now gone to a strange religion;
text_marked: For it becometh not our age, said he, in any wise to dissemble, whereby many young persons might think that Eleazar, being fourscore years old and ten, were now gone to a strange religion;

text: And so they through mine hypocrisy, and desire to live a little time and a moment longer, should be deceived by me, and I get a stain to mine old age, and make it abominable.
text_marked: And so they through mine hypocrisy, and desire to live a little time and a moment longer, should be deceived by me, and I get a stain to mine old age, and make it abominable.

text: For though for the present time I should be delivered from the punishment of men: yet should I not escape the hand of the Almighty, neither alive, nor dead.
text_marked: For though for the present time I should be delivered from the punishment of men: yet should I not escape the hand of the Almighty, neither alive, nor dead.

text: Wherefore now, manfully changing this life, I will shew myself such an one as mine age requireth,
text_marked: Wherefore now, manfully changing this life, I will shew myself such an one as mine age requireth,

text: And leave a notable example to such as be young to die willingly and courageously for the honourable and holy laws. And when he had said these words, immediately he went to the torment:
text_marked: And leave a notable example to such as be young to die willingly and courageously for the honourable and holy laws. And when he had said these words, immediately he went to the torment:

text: They that led him changing the good will they bare him a little before into hatred, because the foresaid speeches proceeded, as they thought, from a desperate mind.
text_marked: They that led him changing the good will they bare him a little before into hatred, because the foresaid speeches proceeded, as they thought, from a desperate mind.

text: But when he was ready to die with stripes, he groaned, and said, It is manifest unto the Lord, that hath the holy knowledge, that whereas I might have been delivered from death, I now endure sore pains in body by being beaten: but in soul am well content to suffer these things, because I fear him.
text_marked: But when he was ready to die with stripes, he groaned, and said, It is manifest unto the Lord, that hath the holy knowledge, that whereas I might have been delivered from death, I now endure sore pains in body by being beaten: but in soul am well content to suffer these things, because I fear him.

text: And thus this man died, leaving his death for an example of a noble courage, and a memorial of virtue, not only unto young men, but unto all his nation.
text_marked: And thus this man died, leaving his death for an example of a noble courage, and a memorial of virtue, not only unto young men, but unto all his nation.

text: It came to pass also, that seven brethren with their mother were taken, and compelled by the king against the law to taste swine’s flesh, and were tormented with scourges and whips.
text_marked: It came to pass also, that seven brethren with their mother were taken, and compelled by the king against the law to taste swine’s flesh, and were tormented with scourges and whips.

text: But one of them that spake first said thus, What wouldest thou ask or learn of us? we are ready to die, rather than to transgress the laws of our fathers.
text_marked: But one of them that spake first said thus, What wouldest thou ask or learn of us? we are ready to die, rather than to transgress the laws of our fathers.

text: Then the king, being in a rage, commanded pans and caldrons to be made hot:
text_marked: Then the king, being in a rage, commanded pans and caldrons to be made hot:

text: Which forthwith being heated, he commanded to cut out the tongue of him that spake first, and to cut off the utmost parts of his body, the rest of his brethren and his mother looking on.
text_marked: Which forthwith being heated, he commanded to cut out the tongue of him that spake first, and to cut off the utmost parts of his body, the rest of his brethren and his mother looking on.

text: Now when he was thus maimed in all his members, he commanded him being yet alive to be brought to the fire, and to be fried in the pan: and as the vapour of the pan was for a good space dispersed, they exhorted one another with the mother to die manfully, saying thus,
text_marked: Now when he was thus maimed in all his members, he commanded him being yet alive to be brought to the fire, and to be fried in the pan: and as the vapour of the pan was for a good space dispersed, they exhorted one another with the mother to die manfully, saying thus,

text: The Lord God looketh upon us, and in truth hath comfort in us, as Moses in his song, which witnessed to their faces, declared, saying, And he shall be comforted in his servants.
text_marked: The Lord God looketh upon us, and in truth hath comfort in us, as Moses in his song, which witnessed to their faces, declared, saying, And he shall be comforted in his servants.

text: So when the first was dead after this manner, they brought the second to make him a mocking stock: and when they had pulled off the skin of his head with the hair, they asked him, Wilt thou eat, before thou be punished throughout every member of thy body?
text_marked: So when the first was dead after this manner, they brought the second to make him a mocking stock: and when they had pulled off the skin of his head with the hair, they asked him, Wilt thou eat, before thou be punished throughout every member of thy body?

text: But he answered in his own language, and said, No. Wherefore he also received the next torment in order, as the former did.
text_marked: But he answered in his own language, and said, No. Wherefore he also received the next torment in order, as the former did.

text: And when he was at the last gasp, he said, Thou like a fury takest us out of this present life, but the King of the world shall raise us up, who have died for his laws, unto everlasting life.
text_marked: And when he was at the last gasp, he said, Thou like a fury takest us out of this present life, but the King of the world shall raise us up, who have died for his laws, unto everlasting life.

text: After him was the third made a mocking stock: and when he was required, he put out his tongue, and that right soon, holding forth his hands manfully.
text_marked: After him was the third made a mocking stock: and when he was required, he put out his tongue, and that right soon, holding forth his hands manfully.

text: And said courageously, These I had from heaven; and for his laws I despise them; and from him I hope to receive them again.
text_marked: And said courageously, These I had from heaven; and for his laws I despise them; and from him I hope to receive them again.

text: Insomuch that the king, and they that were with him, marvelled at the young man’s courage, for that he nothing regarded the pains.

text: Then looked he unto the king, and said, Thou hast power over men, thou art corruptible, thou doest what thou wilt; yet think not that our nation is forsaken of God;

text: After him also they brought the sixth, who being ready to die said, Be not deceived without cause: for we suffer these things for ourselves, having sinned against our God: therefore marvellous things are done unto us.

text: But the mother was marvellous above all, and worthy of honourable memory: for when she saw her seven sons slain within the space of one day, she bare it with a good courage, because of the hope that she had in the Lord.

text: Yea, she exhorted every one of them in her own language, filled with courageous spirits; and stirring up her womanish thoughts with a manly stomach, she said unto them,

text: I cannot tell how ye came into my womb: for I neither gave you breath nor life, neither was it I that formed the members of every one of you;
text_marked: I cannot tell how ye came into my womb: for I neither gave you breath nor life, neither was it I that formed the members of every one of you;

text: But doubtless the Creator of the world, who formed the generation of man, and found out the beginning of all things, will also of his own mercy give you breath and life again, as ye now regard not your own selves for his laws’ sake.
text_marked: But doubtless the Creator of the world, who formed the generation of man, and found out the beginning of all things, will also of his own mercy give you breath and life again, as ye now regard not your own selves for his laws’ sake.

text: Now Antiochus, thinking himself despised, and suspecting it to be a reproachful speech, whilst the youngest was yet alive, did not only exhort him by words, but also assured him with oaths, that he would make him both a rich and a happy man, if he would turn from the laws of his fathers; and that also he would take him for his friend, and trust him with affairs.

text: But she bowing herself toward him, laughing the cruel tyrant to scorn, spake in her country language on this manner; O my son, have pity upon me that bare thee nine months in my womb, and gave thee suck three years, and nourished thee, and brought thee up unto this age, and endured the troubles of education.

text: I beseech thee, my son, look upon the heaven and the earth, and all that is therein, and consider that God made them of things that were not; and so was mankind made likewise.

text: Whiles she was yet speaking these words, the young man said, Whom wait ye for? I will not obey the king’s commandment: but I will obey the commandment of the law that was given unto our fathers by Moses.

text: But thou, O godless man, and of all other most wicked, be not lifted up without a cause, nor puffed up with uncertain hopes, lifting up thy hand against the servants of God:

text: For thou hast not yet escaped the judgment of Almighty God, who seeth all things.
text_marked: For thou hast not yet escaped the judgment of Almighty God, who seeth all things.

text: For our brethren, who now have suffered a short pain, are dead under God’s covenant of everlasting life: but thou, through the judgment of God, shalt receive just punishment for thy pride.

text: But I, as my brethren, offer up my body and life for the laws of our fathers, beseeching God that he would speedily be merciful unto our nation; and that thou by torments and plagues mayest confess, that he alone is God;

text: And that in me and my brethren the wrath of the Almighty, which is justly brought upon our nation, may cease.

text: Then Judas Maccabeus, and they that were with him, went privily into the towns, and called their kinsfolks together, and took unto them all such as continued in the Jews’ religion, and assembled about six thousand men.

text: And they called upon the Lord, that he would look upon the people that was trodden down of all; and also pity the temple profaned of ungodly men;

text: And that he would have compassion upon the city, sore defaced, and ready to be made even with the ground; and hear the blood that cried unto him,

text: Now when Maccabeus had his company about him, he could not be withstood by the heathen: for the wrath of the Lord was turned into mercy.
text_marked: Now when Maccabeus had his company about him, he could not be withstood by the heathen: for the wrath of the Lord was turned into mercy.

text: Therefore he came at unawares, and burnt up towns and cities, and got into his hands the most commodious places, and overcame and put to flight no small number of his enemies.
text_marked: Therefore he came at unawares, and burnt up towns and cities, and got into his hands the most commodious places, and overcame and put to flight no small number of his enemies.

text: But specially took he advantage of the night for such privy attempts, insomuch that the fruit of his holiness was spread every where.

text: So when Philip saw that this man increased by little and little, and that things prospered with him still more and more, he wrote unto Ptolemeus, the governor of Celosyria and Phenice, to yield more aid to the king’s affairs.

text: Then forthwith choosing Nicanor the son of Patroclus, one of his special friends, he sent him with no fewer than twenty thousand of all nations under him, to root out the whole generation of the Jews; and with him he joined also Gorgias a captain, who in matters of war had great experience.

text: So Nicanor undertook to make so much money of the captive Jews, as should defray the tribute of two thousand talents, which the king was to pay to the Romans.
text_marked: So Nicanor undertook to make so much money of the captive Jews, as should defray the tribute of two thousand talents, which the king was to pay to the Romans.

text: Wherefore immediately he sent to the cities upon the sea coast, proclaiming a sale of the captive Jews, and promising that they should have fourscore and ten bodies for one talent, not expecting the vengeance that was to follow upon him from the Almighty God.

text: So Maccabeus called his men together unto the number of six thousand, and exhorted them not to be stricken with terror of the enemy, nor to fear the great multitude of the heathen, who came wrongly against them; but to fight manfully,

text: And thus he that a little afore thought he might command the waves of the sea, (so proud was he beyond the condition of man) and weigh the high mountains in a balance, was now cast on the ground, and carried in an horselitter, shewing forth unto all the manifest power of God.

text: So that the worms rose up out of the body of this wicked man, and whiles he lived in sorrow and pain, his flesh fell away, and the filthiness of his smell was noisome to all his army.

text: We understand also that the Jews would not consent to our father, for to be brought unto the custom of the Gentiles, but had rather keep their own manner of living: for the which cause they require of us, that we should suffer them to live after their own laws.

text_marked: But when Judas his first band came in sight, the enemies, being smitten with fear and terror through the appearing of him who seeth all things, fled amain, one running into this way, another that way, so as that they were often hurt of their own men, and wounded with the points of their own swords.

text: Judas also was very earnest in pursuing them, killing those wicked wretches, of whom he slew about thirty thousand men.
text_marked: Judas also was very earnest in pursuing them, killing those wicked wretches, of whom he slew about thirty thousand men.

text: Moreover Timotheus himself fell into the hands of Dositheus and Sosipater, whom he besought with much craft to let him go with his life, because he had many of the Jews’ parents, and the brethren of some of them, who, if they put him to death, should not be regarded.

text: So when he had assured them with many words that he would restore them without hurt, according to the agreement, they let him go for the saving of their brethren.

text: Then Maccabeus marched forth to Carnion, and to the temple of Atargatis, and there he slew five and twenty thousand persons.

text: And after he had put to flight and destroyed them, Judas removed the host toward Ephron, a strong city, wherein Lysias abode, and a great multitude of divers nations, and the strong young men kept the walls, and defended them mightily: wherein also was great provision of engines and darts.

text: But when Judas and his company had called upon Almighty God, who with his power breaketh the strength of his enemies, they won the city, and slew twenty and five thousand of them that were within,

text: Who came out with three thousand men of foot and four hundred horsemen.

text: At which time Dositheus, one of Bacenor’s company, who was on horseback, and a strong man, was still upon Gorgias, and taking hold of his coat drew him by force; and when he would have taken that cursed man alive, a horseman of Thracia coming upon him smote off his shoulder, so that Gorgias fled unto Marisa.

text: And also in that he perceived that there was great favour laid up for those that died godly, it was an holy and good thought. Whereupon he made a reconciliation for the dead, that they might be delivered from sin.

text: And with him Lysias his protector, and ruler of his affairs, having either of them a Grecian power of footmen, an hundred and ten thousand, and horsemen five thousand and three hundred, and elephants two and twenty, and three hundred chariots armed with hooks.
text_marked: And with him Lysias his protector, and ruler of his affairs, having either of them a Grecian power of footmen, an hundred and ten thousand, and horsemen five thousand and three hundred, and elephants two and twenty, and three hundred chariots armed with hooks.

text: Menelaus also joined himself with them, and with great dissimulation encouraged Antiochus, not for the safeguard of the country, but because he thought to have been made governor.
text_marked: Menelaus also joined himself with them, and with great dissimulation encouraged Antiochus, not for the safeguard of the country, but because he thought to have been made governor.

text: But the King of kings moved Antiochus’ mind against this wicked wretch, and Lysias informed the king that this man was the cause of all mischief, so that the king commanded to bring him unto Berea, and to put him to death, as the manner is in that place.
text_marked: But the King of kings moved Antiochus’ mind against this wicked wretch, and Lysias informed the king that this man was the cause of all mischief, so that the king commanded to bring him unto Berea, and to put him to death, as the manner is in that place.

text: Now there was in that place a tower of fifty cubits high, full of ashes, and it had a round instrument which on every side hanged down into the ashes.
text_marked: Now there was in that place a tower of fifty cubits high, full of ashes, and it had a round instrument which on every side hanged down into the ashes.

text: And whosoever was condemned of sacrilege, or had committed any other grievous crime, there did all men thrust him unto death.
text_marked: And whosoever was condemned of sacrilege, or had committed any other grievous crime, there did all men thrust him unto death.

text: Such a death it happened that wicked man to die, not having so much as burial in the earth; and that most justly:
text_marked: Such a death it happened that wicked man to die, not having so much as burial in the earth; and that most justly:

text: For inasmuch as he had committed many sins about the altar, whose fire and ashes were holy, he received his death in ashes.
text_marked: For inasmuch as he had committed many sins about the altar, whose fire and ashes were holy, he received his death in ashes.

text: Now the king came with a barbarous and haughty mind to do far worse to the Jews, than had been done in his father’s time.
text_marked: Now the king came with a barbarous and haughty mind to do far worse to the Jews, than had been done in his father’s time.

text: Which things when Judas perceived, he commanded the multitude to call upon the Lord night and day, that if ever at any other time, he would now also help them, being at the point to be put from their law, from their country, and from the holy temple:
text_marked: Which things when Judas perceived, he commanded the multitude to call upon the Lord night and day, that if ever at any other time, he would now also help them, being at the point to be put from their law, from their country, and from the holy temple:

text: And that he would not suffer the people, that had even now been but a little refreshed, to be in subjection to the blasphemous nations.

text: So when they had all done this together, and besought the merciful Lord with weeping and fasting, and lying flat upon the ground three days long, Judas, having exhorted them, commanded they should be in a readiness.

text: And Judas, being apart with the elders, determined, before the king’s host should enter into Judea, and get the city, to go forth and try the matter in fight by the help of the Lord.
text_marked: And Judas, being apart with the elders, determined, before the king’s host should enter into Judea, and get the city, to go forth and try the matter in fight by the help of the Lord.

text: So when he had committed all to the Creator of the world, and exhorted his soldiers to fight manfully, even unto death, for the laws, the temple, the city, the country, and the commonwealth, he camped by Modin:
text_marked: So when he had committed all to the Creator of the world, and exhorted his soldiers to fight manfully, even unto death, for the laws, the temple, the city, the country, and the commonwealth, he camped by Modin:

text: And having given the watchword to them that were about him, Victory is of God; with the most valiant and choice young men he went in into the king’s tent by night, and slew in the camp about four thousand men, and the chiefest of the elephants, with all that were upon him.

text: Heard that Philip, who was left over the affairs in Antioch, was desperately bent, confounded, intreated the Jews, submitted himself, and sware to all equal conditions, agreed with them, and offered sacrifice, honoured the temple, and dealt kindly with the place,

text_marked: Lysias went up to the judgment seat, said as much as could be in defence of the cause, persuaded, pacified, made them well affected, returned to Antioch. Thus it went touching the king’s coming and departing.

text: Came to king Demetrius in the hundred and one and fiftieth year, presenting unto him a crown of gold, and a palm, and also of the boughs which were used solemnly in the temple: and so that day he held his peace.

text: Howbeit having gotten opportunity to further his foolish enterprize, and being called into counsel by Demetrius, and asked how the Jews stood affected, and what they intended, he answered thereunto:

text: Those of the Jews that he called Assideans, whose captain is Judas Maccabeus, nourish war and are seditious, and will not let the rest be in peace.
text_marked: Those of the Jews that he called Assideans, whose captain is Judas Maccabeus, nourish war and are seditious, and will not let the rest be in peace.

text: Therefore I, being deprived of mine ancestors’ honour, I mean the high priesthood, am now come hither:
text_marked: Therefore I, being deprived of mine ancestors’ honour, I mean the high priesthood, am now come hither:

text: First, verily for the unfeigned care I have of things pertaining to the king; and secondly, even for that I intend the good of mine own countrymen: for all our nation is in no small misery through the unadvised dealing of them aforersaid.
text_marked: First, verily for the unfeigned care I have of things pertaining to the king; and secondly, even for that I intend the good of mine own countrymen: for all our nation is in no small misery through the unadvised dealing of them aforersaid.

text: Wherefore, O king, seeing knowest all these things, be careful for the country, and our nation, which is pressed on every side, according to the clemency that thou readily shewest unto all.
text_marked: Wherefore, O king, seeing knowest all these things, be careful for the country, and our nation, which is pressed on every side, according to the clemency that thou readily shewest unto all.

text: For as long as Judas liveth, it is not possible that the state should be quiet.
text_marked: For as long as Judas liveth, it is not possible that the state should be quiet.

text: This was no sooner spoken of him, but others of the king’s friends, being maliciously set against Judas, did more incense Demetrius.

text: And forthwith calling Nicanor, who had been master of the elephants, and making him governor over Judea, he sent him forth,

text_marked: Commanding him to slay Judas, and to scatter them that were with him, and to make Alcimus high priest of the great temple.

text: Now when the Jews heard of Nicanor’s coming, and that the heathen were up against them, they cast earth upon their heads, and made supplication to him that had established his people for ever, and who always helpeth his portion with manifestation of his presence.

text_marked: And he would not willingly have Judas out of his sight: for he love the man from his heart

text: But Alcimus, perceiving the love that was betwixt them, and considering the covenants that were made, came to Demetrius, and told him that Nicanor was not well affected toward the state; for that he had ordained Judas, a traitor to his realm, to be the king’s successor.

text: Then the king being in a rage, and provoked with the accusations of the most wicked man, wrote to Nicanor, signifying that he was much displeased with the covenants, and commanding him that he should send Maccabeus prisoner in all haste unto Antioch.

text: Until the land had enjoyed her sabbaths, the whole time of her desolation shall she rest, until the full term of seventy years.
text_marked: Until the land had enjoyed her sabbaths, the whole time of her desolation shall she rest, until the full term of seventy years.

text: In the first year of Cyrus king of the Persians, that the word of the Lord might be accomplished, that he had promised by the mouth of Jeremy;
text_marked: In the first year of Cyrus king of the Persians, that the word of the Lord might be accomplished, that he had promised by the mouth of Jeremy;

text: The Lord raised up the spirit of Cyrus the king of the Persians, and he made proclamation through all his kingdom, and also by writing,
text_marked: The Lord raised up the spirit of Cyrus the king of the Persians, and he made proclamation through all his kingdom, and also by writing,

text: Saying, Thus saith Cyrus king of the Persians; The Lord of Israel, the most high Lord, hath made me king of the whole world,
text_marked: Saying, Thus saith Cyrus king of the Persians; The Lord of Israel, the most high Lord, hath made me king of the whole world,

text: And commanded me to build him an house at Jerusalem in Jewry.
text_marked: And commanded me to build him an house at Jerusalem in Jewry.

text: If therefore there be any of you that are of his people, let the Lord, even his Lord, be with him, and let him go up to Jerusalem that is in Judea, and build the house of the Lord of Israel: for he is the Lord that dwelleth in Jerusalem.
text_marked: If therefore there be any of you that are of his people, let the Lord, even his Lord, be with him, and let him go up to Jerusalem that is in Judea, and build the house of the Lord of Israel: for he is the Lord that dwelleth in Jerusalem.

text: Whosoever then dwell in the places about, let them help him, those, I say, that are his neighbours, with gold, and with silver,
text_marked: Whosoever then dwell in the places about, let them help him, those, I say, that are his neighbours, with gold, and with silver,

text: With gifts, with horses, and with cattle, and other things, which have been set forth by vow, for the temple of the Lord at Jerusalem.
text_marked: With gifts, with horses, and with cattle, and other things, which have been set forth by vow, for the temple of the Lord at Jerusalem.

text: Then the chief of the families of Judea and of the tribe of Benjamin stood up; the priests also, and the Levites, and all they whose mind the Lord had moved to go up, and to build an house for the Lord at Jerusalem,
text_marked: Then the chief of the families of Judea and of the tribe of Benjamin stood up; the priests also, and the Levites, and all they whose mind the Lord had moved to go up, and to build an house for the Lord at Jerusalem,

text: And they that dwelt round about them, and helped them in all things with silver and gold, with horses and cattle, and with very many free gifts of a great number whose minds were stirred up thereto.
text_marked: And they that dwelt round about them, and helped them in all things with silver and gold, with horses and cattle, and with very many free gifts of a great number whose minds were stirred up thereto.

text: King Cyrus also brought forth the holy vessels, which Nabuchodonosor had carried away from Jerusalem, and had set up in his temple of idols.
text_marked: King Cyrus also brought forth the holy vessels, which Nabuchodonosor had carried away from Jerusalem, and had set up in his temple of idols.

text: Now when Cyrus king of the Persians had brought them forth, he delivered them to Mithridates his treasurer:
text_marked: Now when Cyrus king of the Persians had brought them forth, he delivered them to Mithridates his treasurer:

text: And by him they were delivered to Sanabassar the governor of Judea.
text_marked: And by him they were delivered to Sanabassar the governor of Judea.

text: And this was the number of them; A thousand golden cups, and a thousand of silver, censers of silver twenty nine, vials of gold thirty, and of silver two thousand four hundred and ten, and a thousand other vessels.
text_marked: And this was the number of them; A thousand golden cups, and a thousand of silver, censers of silver twenty nine, vials of gold thirty, and of silver two thousand four hundred and ten, and a thousand other vessels.

text: So all the vessels of gold and of silver, which were carried away, were five thousand four hundred threescore and nine.
text_marked: So all the vessels of gold and of silver, which were carried away, were five thousand four hundred threescore and nine.

text: These were brought back by Sanabassar, together with them of the captivity, from Babylon to Jerusalem.
text_marked: These were brought back by Sanabassar, together with them of the captivity, from Babylon to Jerusalem.

text: But in the time of Artexerxes king of the Persians Belemus, and Mithridates, and Tabellius, and Rathumus, and Beeltethmus, and Semellius the secretary, with others that were in commission with them, dwelling in Samaria and other places, wrote unto him against them that dwelt in Judea and Jerusalem these letters following;
text_marked: But in the time of Artexerxes king of the Persians Belemus, and Mithridates, and Tabellius, and Rathumus, and Beeltethmus, and Semellius the secretary, with others that were in commission with them, dwelling in Samaria and other places, wrote unto him against them that dwelt in Judea and Jerusalem these letters following;

text: To king Artexerxes our lord, Thy servants, Rathumus the storywriter, and Semellius the scribe, and the rest of their council, and the judges that are in Celosyria and Phenice.
text_marked: To king Artexerxes our lord, Thy servants, Rathumus the storywriter, and Semellius the scribe, and the rest of their council, and the judges that are in Celosyria and Phenice.

text: Be it now known to the lord king, that the Jews that are up from you to us, being come into Jerusalem, that rebellious and wicked city, do build the marketplaces, and repair the walls of it and do lay the foundation of the temple.
text_marked: Be it now known to the lord king, that the Jews that are up from you to us, being come into Jerusalem, that rebellious and wicked city, do build the marketplaces, and repair the walls of it and do lay the foundation of the temple.

text: Now if this city and the walls thereof be made up again, they will not only refuse to give tribute, but also rebel against kings.
text_marked: Now if this city and the walls thereof be made up again, they will not only refuse to give tribute, but also rebel against kings.

text: And forasmuch as the things pertaining to the temple are now in hand, we think it meet not to neglect such a matter,
text_marked: And forasmuch as the things pertaining to the temple are now in hand, we think it meet not to neglect such a matter,

text: But to speak unto our lord the king, to the intent that, if it be thy pleasure it may be sought out in the books of thy fathers:
text_marked: But to speak unto our lord the king, to the intent that, if it be thy pleasure it may be sought out in the books of thy fathers:

text: And thou shalt find in the chronicles what is written concerning these things, and shalt understand that that city was rebellious, troubling both kings and cities:
text_marked: And thou shalt find in the chronicles what is written concerning these things, and shalt understand that that city was rebellious, troubling both kings and cities:

text: And that the Jews were rebellious, and raised always wars therein; for the which cause even this city was made desolate.
text_marked: And that the Jews were rebellious, and raised always wars therein; for the which cause even this city was made desolate.

text: Wherefore now we do declare unto thee, O lord the king, that if this city be built again, and the walls thereof set up anew, thou shalt from henceforth have no passage into Celosyria and Phenice.
text_marked: Wherefore now we do declare unto thee, O lord the king, that if this city be built again, and the walls thereof set up anew, thou shalt from henceforth have no passage into Celosyria and Phenice.

text: Then the king wrote back again to Rathumus the storywriter, to Beeltethmus, to Semellius the scribe, and to the rest that were in commission, and dwellers in Samaria and Syria and Phenice, after this manner;
text_marked: Then the king wrote back again to Rathumus the storywriter, to Beeltethmus, to Semellius the scribe, and to the rest that were in commission, and dwellers in Samaria and Syria and Phenice, after this manner;

text: I have read the epistle which ye have sent unto me: therefore I commanded to make diligent search, and it hath been found that that city was from the beginning practising against kings;
text_marked: I have read the epistle which ye have sent unto me: therefore I commanded to make diligent search, and it hath been found that that city was from the beginning practising against kings;

text: And the men therein were given to rebellion and war: and that mighty kings and fierce were in Jerusalem, who reigned and exacted tributes in Celosyria and Phenice.
text_marked: And the men therein were given to rebellion and war: and that mighty kings and fierce were in Jerusalem, who reigned and exacted tributes in Celosyria and Phenice.

text: Now therefore I have commanded to hinder those men from building the city, and heed to be taken that there be no more done in it;
text_marked: Now therefore I have commanded to hinder those men from building the city, and heed to be taken that there be no more done in it;

text: And that those wicked workers proceed no further to the annoyance of kings,
text_marked: And that those wicked workers proceed no further to the annoyance of kings,

text: Then king Artexerxes his letters being read, Rathumus, and Semellius the scribe, and the rest that were in commission with them, removing in haste toward Jerusalem with a troop of horsemen and a multitude of people in battle array, began to hinder the builders; and the building of the temple in Jerusalem ceased until the second year of the reign of Darius king of the Persians.
text_marked: Then king Artexerxes his letters being read, Rathumus, and Semellius the scribe, and the rest that were in commission with them, removing in haste toward Jerusalem with a troop of horsemen and a multitude of people in battle array, began to hinder the builders; and the building of the temple in Jerusalem ceased until the second year of the reign of Darius king of the Persians.

text: Now when Darius reigned, he made a great feast unto all his subjects, and unto all his household, and unto all the princes of Media and Persia,
text_marked: Now when Darius reigned, he made a great feast unto all his subjects, and unto all his household, and unto all the princes of Media and Persia,

text: And to all the governors and captains and lieutenants that were under him, from India unto Ethiopia, of an hundred twenty and seven provinces.
text_marked: And to all the governors and captains and lieutenants that were under him, from India unto Ethiopia, of an hundred twenty and seven provinces.

text: And when they had eaten and drunken, and being satisfied were gone home, then Darius the king went into his bedchamber, and slept, and soon after awaked.
text_marked: And when they had eaten and drunken, and being satisfied were gone home, then Darius the king went into his bedchamber, and slept, and soon after awaked.

text: Then three young men, that were of the guard that kept the king’s body, spake one to another;
text_marked: Then three young men, that were of the guard that kept the king’s body, spake one to another;

text: Let every one of us speak a sentence: he that shall overcome, and whose sentence shall seem wiser than the others, unto him shall the king Darius give great gifts, and great things in token of victory:
text_marked: Let every one of us speak a sentence: he that shall overcome, and whose sentence shall seem wiser than the others, unto him shall the king Darius give great gifts, and great things in token of victory:

text: As, to be clothed in purple, to drink in gold, and to sleep upon gold, and a chariot with bridles of gold, and an headtire of fine linen, and a chain about his neck:
text_marked: As, to be clothed in purple, to drink in gold, and to sleep upon gold, and a chariot with bridles of gold, and an headtire of fine linen, and a chain about his neck:

text: And he shall sit next to Darius because of his wisdom, and shall be called Darius his cousin.
text_marked: And he shall sit next to Darius because of his wisdom, and shall be called Darius his cousin.

text: And then every one wrote his sentence, sealed it, and laid it under king Darius his pillow;
text_marked: And then every one wrote his sentence, sealed it, and laid it under king Darius his pillow;

text: And said that, when the king is risen, some will give him the writings; and of whose side the king and the three princes of Persia shall judge that his sentence is the wisest, to him shall the victory be given, as was appointed.
text_marked: And said that, when the king is risen, some will give him the writings; and of whose side the king and the three princes of Persia shall judge that his sentence is the wisest, to him shall the victory be given, as was appointed.

text: The first wrote, Wine is the strongest.
text_marked: The first wrote, Wine is the strongest.

text: The second wrote, The king is strongest.
text_marked: The second wrote, The king is strongest.

text: The third wrote, Women are strongest: but above all things Truth beareth away the victory.
text_marked: The third wrote, Women are strongest: but above all things Truth beareth away the victory.

text: Now when the king was risen up, they took their writings, and delivered them unto him, and so he read them:
text_marked: Now when the king was risen up, they took their writings, and delivered them unto him, and so he read them:

text: And sending forth he called all the princes of Persia and Media, and the governors, and the captains, and the lieutenants, and the chief officers;
text_marked: And sending forth he called all the princes of Persia and Media, and the governors, and the captains, and the lieutenants, and the chief officers;

text: And sat him down in the royal seat of judgment; and the writings were read before them.
text_marked: And sat him down in the royal seat of judgment; and the writings were read before them.

text: And he said, Call the young men, and they shall declare their own sentences. So they were called, and came in.
text_marked: And he said, Call the young men, and they shall declare their own sentences. So they were called, and came in.

text: And he said unto them, Declare unto us your mind concerning the writings. Then began the first, who had spoken of the strength of wine;
text_marked: And he said unto them, Declare unto us your mind concerning the writings. Then began the first, who had spoken of the strength of wine;

text: And he said thus, O ye men, how exceeding strong is wine! it causeth all men to err that drink it:
text_marked: And he said thus, O ye men, how exceeding strong is wine! it causeth all men to err that drink it:

text: It maketh the mind of the king and of the fatherless child to be all one; of the bondman and of the freeman, of the poor man and of the rich:
text_marked: It maketh the mind of the king and of the fatherless child to be all one; of the bondman and of the freeman, of the poor man and of the rich:

text: It turneth also every thought into jollity and mirth, so that a man remembereth neither sorrow nor debt:
text_marked: It turneth also every thought into jollity and mirth, so that a man remembereth neither sorrow nor debt:

text: And it maketh every heart rich, so that a man remembereth neither king nor governor; and it maketh to speak all things by talents:
text_marked: And it maketh every heart rich, so that a man remembereth neither king nor governor; and it maketh to speak all things by talents:

text: And when they are in their cups, they forget their love both to friends and brethren, and a little after draw out swords:
text_marked: And when they are in their cups, they forget their love both to friends and brethren, and a little after draw out swords:

text: But when they are from the wine, they remember not what they have done.
text_marked: But when they are from the wine, they remember not what they have done.

text: O ye men, is not wine the strongest, that enforceth to do thus? And when he had so spoken, he held his peace.
text_marked: O ye men, is not wine the strongest, that enforceth to do thus? And when he had so spoken, he held his peace.

text: Then the second, that had spoken of the strength of the king, began to say,
text_marked: Then the second, that had spoken of the strength of the king, began to say,

text: O ye men, do not men excel in strength that bear rule over sea and land and all things in them?
text_marked: O ye men, do not men excel in strength that bear rule over sea and land and all things in them?

text: But yet the king is more mighty: for he is lord of all these things, and hath dominion over them; and whatsoever he commandeth them they do.
text_marked: But yet the king is more mighty: for he is lord of all these things, and hath dominion over them; and whatsoever he commandeth them they do.

text: If he bid them make war the one against the other, they do it: if he send them out against the enemies, they go, and break down mountains walls and towers.
text_marked: If he bid them make war the one against the other, they do it: if he send them out against the enemies, they go, and break down mountains walls and towers.

text: They slay and are slain, and transgress not the king’s commandment: if they get the victory, they bring all to the king, as well the spoil, as all things else.
text_marked: They slay and are slain, and transgress not the king’s commandment: if they get the victory, they bring all to the king, as well the spoil, as all things else.

text: Likewise for those that are no soldiers, and have not to do with wars, but use husbundry, when they have reaped again that which they had sown, they bring it to the king, and compel one another to pay tribute unto the king.
text_marked: Likewise for those that are no soldiers, and have not to do with wars, but use husbundry, when they have reaped again that which they had sown, they bring it to the king, and compel one another to pay tribute unto the king.

text: And yet he is but one man: if he command to kill, they kill; if he command to spare, they spare;
text_marked: And yet he is but one man: if he command to kill, they kill; if he command to spare, they spare;

text: If he command to smite, they smite; if he command to make desolate, they make desolate; if he command to build, they build;
text_marked: If he command to smite, they smite; if he command to make desolate, they make desolate; if he command to build, they build;

text: If he command to cut down, they cut down; if he command to plant, they plant.
text_marked: If he command to cut down, they cut down; if he command to plant, they plant.

text: So all his people and his armies obey him: furthermore he lieth down, he eateth and drinketh, and taketh his rest:
text_marked: So all his people and his armies obey him: furthermore he lieth down, he eateth and drinketh, and taketh his rest:

text: And these keep watch round about him, neither may any one depart, and do his own business, neither disobey they him in any thing.
text_marked: And these keep watch round about him, neither may any one depart, and do his own business, neither disobey they him in any thing.

text: O ye men, how should not the king be mightiest, when in such sort he is obeyed? And he held his tongue.
text_marked: O ye men, how should not the king be mightiest, when in such sort he is obeyed? And he held his tongue.

text: Then the third, who had spoken of women, and of the truth, (this was Zorobabel) began to speak.
text_marked: Then the third, who had spoken of women, and of the truth, (this was Zorobabel) began to speak.

text: O ye men, it is not the great king, nor the multitude of men, neither is it wine, that excelleth; who is it then that ruleth them, or hath the lordship over them? are they not women?
text_marked: O ye men, it is not the great king, nor the multitude of men, neither is it wine, that excelleth; who is it then that ruleth them, or hath the lordship over them? are they not women?

text: Women have borne the king and all the people that bear rule by sea and land.
text_marked: Women have borne the king and all the people that bear rule by sea and land.

text: Even of them came they: and they nourished them up that planted the vineyards, from whence the wine cometh.
text_marked: Even of them came they: and they nourished them up that planted the vineyards, from whence the wine cometh.

text: These also make garments for men; these bring glory unto men; and without women cannot men be.
text_marked: These also make garments for men; these bring glory unto men; and without women cannot men be.

text: Yea, and if men have gathered together gold and silver, or any other goodly thing, do they not love a woman which is comely in favour and beauty?
text_marked: Yea, and if men have gathered together gold and silver, or any other goodly thing, do they not love a woman which is comely in favour and beauty?

text: And letting all those things go, do they not gape, and even with open mouth fix their eyes fast on her; and have not all men more desire unto her than unto silver or gold, or any goodly thing whatsoever?
text_marked: And letting all those things go, do they not gape, and even with open mouth fix their eyes fast on her; and have not all men more desire unto her than unto silver or gold, or any goodly thing whatsoever?

text: A man leaveth his own father that brought him up, and his own country, and cleaveth unto his wife.
text_marked: A man leaveth his own father that brought him up, and his own country, and cleaveth unto his wife.

text: He sticketh not to spend his life with his wife. and remembereth neither father, nor mother, nor country.
text_marked: He sticketh not to spend his life with his wife. and remembereth neither father, nor mother, nor country.

text: By this also ye must know that women have dominion over you: do ye not labour and toil, and give and bring all to the woman?
text_marked: By this also ye must know that women have dominion over you: do ye not labour and toil, and give and bring all to the woman?

text: Yea, a man taketh his sword, and goeth his way to rob and to steal, to sail upon the sea and upon rivers;
text_marked: Yea, a man taketh his sword, and goeth his way to rob and to steal, to sail upon the sea and upon rivers;

text: And looketh upon a lion, and goeth in the darkness; and when he hath stolen, spoiled, and robbed, he bringeth it to his love.
text_marked: And looketh upon a lion, and goeth in the darkness; and when he hath stolen, spoiled, and robbed, he bringeth it to his love.

text: Wherefore a man loveth his wife better than father or mother.
text_marked: Wherefore a man loveth his wife better than father or mother.

text: Yea, many there be that have run out of their wits for women, and become servants for their sakes.
text_marked: Yea, many there be that have run out of their wits for women, and become servants for their sakes.

text: Many also have perished, have erred, and sinned, for women.
text_marked: Many also have perished, have erred, and sinned, for women.

text: And now do ye not believe me? is not the king great in his power? do not all regions fear to touch him?
text_marked: And now do ye not believe me? is not the king great in his power? do not all regions fear to touch him?

text: Yet did I see him and Apame the king’s concubine, the daughter of the admirable Bartacus, sitting at the right hand of the king,
text_marked: Yet did I see him and Apame the king’s concubine, the daughter of the admirable Bartacus, sitting at the right hand of the king,

text: And taking the crown from the king’s head, and setting it upon her own head; she also struck the king with her left hand.
text_marked: And taking the crown from the king’s head, and setting it upon her own head; she also struck the king with her left hand.

text: And yet for all this the king gaped and gazed upon her with open mouth: if she laughed upon him, he laughed also: but if she took any displeasure at him, the king was fain to flatter, that she might be reconciled to him again.
text_marked: And yet for all this the king gaped and gazed upon her with open mouth: if she laughed upon him, he laughed also: but if she took any displeasure at him, the king was fain to flatter, that she might be reconciled to him again.

text: O ye men, how can it be but women should be strong, seeing they do thus?
text_marked: O ye men, how can it be but women should be strong, seeing they do thus?

text: Then the king and the princes looked one upon another: so he began to speak of the truth.
text_marked: Then the king and the princes looked one upon another: so he began to speak of the truth.

text: O ye men, are not women strong? great is the earth, high is the heaven, swift is the sun in his course, for he compasseth the heavens round about, and fetcheth his course again to his own place in one day.
text_marked: O ye men, are not women strong? great is the earth, high is the heaven, swift is the sun in his course, for he compasseth the heavens round about, and fetcheth his course again to his own place in one day.

text: Is he not great that maketh these things? therefore great is the truth, and stronger than all things.
text_marked: Is he not great that maketh these things? therefore great is the truth, and stronger than all things.

text: All the earth crieth upon the truth, and the heaven blesseth it: all works shake and tremble at it, and with it is no unrighteous thing.
text_marked: All the earth crieth upon the truth, and the heaven blesseth it: all works shake and tremble at it, and with it is no unrighteous thing.

text: Wine is wicked, the king is wicked, women are wicked, all the children of men are wicked, and such are all their wicked works; and there is no truth in them; in their unrighteousness also they shall perish.
text_marked: Wine is wicked, the king is wicked, women are wicked, all the children of men are wicked, and such are all their wicked works; and there is no truth in them; in their unrighteousness also they shall perish.

text: As for the truth, it endureth, and is always strong; it liveth and conquereth for evermore.
text_marked: As for the truth, it endureth, and is always strong; it liveth and conquereth for evermore.

text: With her there is no accepting of persons or rewards; but she doeth the things that are just, and refraineth from all unjust and wicked things; and all men do well like of her works.
text_marked: With her there is no accepting of persons or rewards; but she doeth the things that are just, and refraineth from all unjust and wicked things; and all men do well like of her works.

text: Neither in her judgment is any unrighteousness; and she is the strength, kingdom, power, and majesty, of all ages. Blessed be the God of truth.
text_marked: Neither in her judgment is any unrighteousness; and she is the strength, kingdom, power, and majesty, of all ages. Blessed be the God of truth.

text: And with that he held his peace. And all the people then shouted, and said, Great is Truth, and mighty above all things.
text_marked: And with that he held his peace. And all the people then shouted, and said, Great is Truth, and mighty above all things.

text: Then said the king unto him, Ask what thou wilt more than is appointed in the writing, and we will give it thee, because thou art found wisest; and thou shalt sit next me, and shalt be called my cousin.
text_marked: Then said the king unto him, Ask what thou wilt more than is appointed in the writing, and we will give it thee, because thou art found wisest; and thou shalt sit next me, and shalt be called my cousin.

text: Then said he unto the king, Remember thy vow, which thou hast vowed to build Jerusalem, in the day when thou camest to thy kingdom,
text_marked: Then said he unto the king, Remember thy vow, which thou hast vowed to build Jerusalem, in the day when thou camest to thy kingdom,

text: And to send away all the vessels that were taken away out of Jerusalem, which Cyrus set apart, when he vowed to destroy Babylon, and to send them again thither.
text_marked: And to send away all the vessels that were taken away out of Jerusalem, which Cyrus set apart, when he vowed to destroy Babylon, and to send them again thither.

text: Thou also hast vowed to build up the temple, which the Edomites burned when Judea was made desolate by the Chaldees.
text_marked: Thou also hast vowed to build up the temple, which the Edomites burned when Judea was made desolate by the Chaldees.

text: And now, O lord the king, this is that which I require, and which I desire of thee, and this is the princely liberality proceeding from thyself: I desire therefore that thou make good the vow, the performance whereof with thine own mouth thou hast vowed to the King of heaven.
text_marked: And now, O lord the king, this is that which I require, and which I desire of thee, and this is the princely liberality proceeding from thyself: I desire therefore that thou make good the vow, the performance whereof with thine own mouth thou hast vowed to the King of heaven.

text: Then Darius the king stood up, and kissed him, and wrote letters for him unto all the treasurers and lieutenants and captains and governors, that they should safely convey on their way both him, and all those that go up with him to build Jerusalem.
text_marked: Then Darius the king stood up, and kissed him, and wrote letters for him unto all the treasurers and lieutenants and captains and governors, that they should safely convey on their way both him, and all those that go up with him to build Jerusalem.

text: He wrote letters also unto the lieutenants that were in Celosyria and Phenice, and unto them in Libanus, that they should bring cedar wood from Libanus unto Jerusalem, and that they should build the city with him.
text_marked: He wrote letters also unto the lieutenants that were in Celosyria and Phenice, and unto them in Libanus, that they should bring cedar wood from Libanus unto Jerusalem, and that they should build the city with him.

text: Moreover he wrote for all the Jews that went out of his realm up into Jewry, concerning their freedom, that no officer, no ruler, no lieutenant, nor treasurer, should forcibly enter into their doors;
text_marked: Moreover he wrote for all the Jews that went out of his realm up into Jewry, concerning their freedom, that no officer, no ruler, no lieutenant, nor treasurer, should forcibly enter into their doors;

text: And that all the country which they hold should be free without tribute; and that the Edomites should give over the villages of the Jews which then they held:
text_marked: And that all the country which they hold should be free without tribute; and that the Edomites should give over the villages of the Jews which then they held:

text: Yea, that there should be yearly given twenty talents to the building of the temple, until the time that it were built;
text_marked: Yea, that there should be yearly given twenty talents to the building of the temple, until the time that it were built;
